Recommendation
1.3 Modernisation of Police Forces
1.3.1 The Committee takes note of the Mid-Term evaluation of the Modernisation of State Police
Forces Scheme by BPR&D. One of the findings made by the BPR&D in the Study which causes
concern to the Committee is that more than 50 per cent of the fund is utilized in the police housing
and police building activities. The Committee is of the view that with the new technological
advances taking place in a feverish pitch and in view of the fact that the Police Forces in India
function with age-old equipments and gadgets, much of the scheme of modernization should
concentrate on providing modern gadgets, improving technology, providing IT facilities etc.
Spending more than 50 per cent on building activities defeats the very purpose of the Scheme. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs may review the
scheme in the light of pattern of expenditure incurred by the States and prepare a list of activities
which should lay thrust on improving technology and providing modern gadgets, etc.
(Para 15.6)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The concerns expressed by the Committee regarding large amount of funds being utilized
for police housing and police building activities and the need for giving mere emphasis on induction
of modern technology is appreciated and duly noted. Accordingly, in the meetings held in the
Ministry for considering the Annual Action Plans, under the Scheme for Modernisation of State

4
Police Forces (MPF) for the year 2007-08, the State Gevernments were advised to rationalize the
allocation on police housing, etc., and to lay greater emphasis on other aspects of police
modernization such as procurement of modern gadgetry, sophisticated equipments/weaponry etc.
1.3.3 In this regard, it may be noted that the Annual Action Plans under the Scheme for
Modernisation of State Police Forces (MPF) are formulated by the State Governments after
assessing their urgent local requirements. These plans are discussed in the meetings held by the
Central Level High Powered Committee, which are attended by the State representatives also. All
critical items like construction of residential/non-residential buildings, modern weaponry, vehicles,
communication equipment, office equipment, surveillance/intelligence/security equipments, training
facilities, forensic science equipment etc. are covered under the Scheme. Construction of police
station buildings and residential buildings (barracks) for lower subordinates are major components
of the scheme. These are also considered essential as they enhance the morale of the State Police
Forces and are therefore, directly concerned with their efficiency. The improvement in police
performance due to modernization, to a considerable extent, will also depend on the provision of
the basic necessary infrastructure in all the police stations as well as in the district police
headquarters.
1.3.4 Emphasis is also being laid on providing IT facilities. A Project called “Common Integrated
Police Application” (CIPA) is being implemented in all the States to ensure a uniform framework
and mechanism for computerization of the crime registration, investigation, etc. at the police station
level. NIC is the implementing agency for the project, which is being implemented in all the States
in a phased manner.
1.3.5 The Ministry is now planning major thrust on technology upgradation in the functioning of
police at all levels. This is proposed to be done by widening the scope of the CIPA project in terms
of the applications and by extending it from the police stations to the other higher level formations
in the police hierarchy e.g. the circle/districts/range/zonal offices and the police headquarters, for
consolidating the police station databases at a central location and providing appropriate software
interfaces for interaction and sharing of crime related information. At present, CIPA essentially has
crime registration, investigation and prosecution modules. It is now proposed to provide all
functionalities and integrate appropriate technologies, such as, fingerprinting and other forensic
science applications in a large network, so that the information and technology can be shared by
all concerned. For this purpose, the police stations and other higher police formations are also
proposed to be linked through a broadband/CDMA/VSAT network. A comprehensive composite
proposal has been sent to the Planning Commission for including the project under the Eleventh
Five Year Plan (2007-12). When accepted, larger share of funds shall become available within the
Modernisation of Police Forces (non-plan Scheme) for spending on the other essential requirements
like modem weaponry, equipment, construction of secure police stations, etc.
Further Recommendation
1.3.6 The Committee notes that the Ministry of Home Affairs has forwarded the
“Comprehensive Composite Proposal” to the Planning Commission for technology
upgradation in the functioning of police at all level through a pr oject called CIPA—crime
registration, investigation, and prosecution modules to be linked through a broadband/
CDMA/VSAT network. The Committee desires that the Planning Commission may clear the
project at the earliest.

1.6.1 The Committee is given to understand that Special Branches in States/UTs Police Forces

and gadgets, etc. In view of the current internal security situation and the growing naxalite and
terrorist activities, strengthening and modernization of Special branches acquire. significance.The
Committee, therefore, feels that the Special Branches in the States/Union Territories Police Forces
need to be revamped by enhancing their manpower by way of filling up of vacancies by posting
of competent officers with reasonable tenure, dedicated staff for intelligence work right upto the
police station level and reactivating beat constable system and above all making available modern
equipment and gadgets for interception and special training for personnel posted therein.
1.6.2 The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs may impress upon
the State/Union Territories Governments/Administrations to strengthening their Special Branches.

Scheme for strengthening and modernization of Special Branches.

2.1.2 Department of Ocean Development (DOD), Ministry of Earth Sciences is setting up

2.1.3 The progress is being monitored and as per the latest report submitted by Ministry of Earth

in Indian Ocean and Data from 2 Bottom Pressure Reorders and 5 Surface Buoy Systems out of
12 envisaged to be placed in Indian Ocean (Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea) is being received. As

Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), has been established and at present real-time data is being

2.1.4 As against total budget outlay of this project i.e. Rs.125 crore, Rs.87 crore have already

Recommendation
2.2 Naxalism
2.2.1 The Committee also reiterates its observation made earlier that the naxal problem is no
longer a problem of a few States. It has acquired a national dimension posing gravest threat to the
national security. The naxal activities have spread to more than twelve States and are reported to
be having links with external agencies including ISI. The Committee is therefore, of the considered
view that taking into account the growth and influence of the Naxal groups in several States and
the grave threat posed by it to the internal security of the country, it is high time that the Ministry
constitute a Unified Command to effectively tackle the menace. Besides the Central Paramilitary
Forces, State Police Forces may also contribute to the Unified Command. The Committee also
takes note of the observation made by the Home Secretary that naxal attacks on several occasions
take place due to non-observance of ‘Standard Operating Procedure’ (SOP) by the State Police
13

14
Forces. The Committee therefore, strongly recommends that Government may consider creating a
Unified Command common to all the naxal affected States.
(Para 14.6)
Action Taken
2.2.2 Law and Order is a State subject. The Central Government is supplementing the efforts and
resources of the State Governments through a variety of measures, including deployment of Central
Para Military Forces which work under the command of the concerned State Governments,
strengthening of the local Police and Intelligence agencies through the Scheme for Modernisation
of State Police Forces, provision of financial assistance through the Scheme of Security Related
Expenditure, sharing of Intelligence and bringing about inter-State coordination.
1.2.3 For review, coordination and evaluation of the naxalite situation, among other institutional
mechanisms like an Empowered Group of Ministers under the chairmanship of Union Home
Minister with Chief Ministers of concerned States as special invitees and a Coordination Centre
under the Chairmanship of Union Home Secretary, a Task Force under Special Secretary (Internal
Security), consisting of officers of Intelligence agencies, Central Para Military Forces and
concerned State Police Forces, has also been set up to deliberate upon the various steps needed
to deal with the activities of naxalites and to bring about co-ordination between authorities of
different States as may be necessary.
1.2.4 The system of a Unified Command can be implemented within a particular State, as has
been done in some States affected by violence (for example, Jammu and Kashmir) with the
objective of ensuring coordination between State and Central agencies involved in internal security
duties within the State. Any such mechanism. is not constitutionally or otherwise feasible with
reference to multiple States being brought under any kind of a unified command. However, the
need for inter-State coordination has been fully recognized, and that is the reason for setting up

Recommendation
3.1 Relief and rehabilitation measures for J&K migrants

Since the State Government could not utilize the allocated amount, a sum of Rs.12 crore remained

now been informed by the State Government that the stay granted by the Court has since been

Migrants resulting in the better utilization of funds this year.

18
3.1.5 To further facilitate the State Government in improving their fiscal management, a special
audit of SRE related expenditure has been undertaken. The ongoing scheme for return of Kashmiri
Migrants, such as two-room flats at Budgam are being expedited for which Rs.18 crore has

3.2 Coastal Security Scheme
3.2.1 The Committee feels that as there is a greater risk of infiltration from coastal belts, the
scheme needs to be implemented in the right earnest. This requires co-operation of all the States.
However, the Committee is constrained to note that some of the States have not yet sanctioned
the manpower. The Ministry may impress upon the State Governments concerned to take early
action in the matter. The Committee also recommends that the process of acquiring boats may be
completed at the earliest, as they are an essential component for coastal security surveillance. In

for implementation in 5 years commencing from 2005-06. The progress in the implementation of
the Scheme is being monitored periodically by this Ministry.
3.2.3 Under the Scheme, manpower is to be provided by the States and Union Territories.
Manpower for the executive posts has been sanctioned by all the States. Manpower for the

Karnataka, Goa, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Proposal for sanction of

coasts, respectively.
3.2.5 A Price Negotiation Committee (PNC) has been constituted under Joint Secretary (PM),
MHA to arrive at a negotiated price for the boats. The PNC has held discussions on
15th November, 2006, 4th January, 2007, 2nd March, 2007, 13th April, 2007 and 5th July, 2007.
The price negotiations, in progress, are at the final stages.

19
Further Recommendation
3.2.6 The Committee is constrained to note that even though the scheme was approved in
2005 for implementation in five years several proposals are still in approval stage. The
Committee recommends that all the proposals may be given approval at the earliest. The
Committee also recommends that the Price Negotiation Committee of MHA may complete
all the formalities for purchase of boats.

3.3 National Disaster Management Authority
3.3.1 Similarly, the Committee also expresses its concern over the slow pace in the formulation
of National Policy on Disaster Management. The Committee takes a strong exception on the delay
and recommends that Government should finalise the policy at the earliest.
(Para 11.8)
Action Taken
3.3.2 A draft of the National Policy on Disaster Management has been prepared by the National
Disaster Management Authority. The same is being considered by this Ministry, inter-alia, in the
light of the recommendations contained in the 3rd Report of the 2nd Administrative Reforms
Commission (ARC) titled ‘Crisis Management – From Despair to Hope’, which contains a number
of recommendations on disaster management and a decision on these recommendations will also
have a bearing on the National Policy.
Further Recommendation
3.3.3 The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should expeditiously
consider the Draft National Policy on Disaster Management as prepared by the National
Disaster Management Authority and finalize the policy at the earliest. The country can not
wait for a disaster to happen before the policy is finalized.
Recommendation
3.4 National Disaster Management Authority
3.4.1 The Committee has also been infonned that the Disaster Response Fund and Disaster
Mitigation Fund have not so far been constituted. It shows the lax attitude of the Ministry in
constituting such important funds for which the legislation was passed in 2005 itself. The
Committee disapproves of this laxity and recommends that steps may be taken for immediate
constitution of the funds.
(Para 11.11)
Action Taken
I. National Disaster Response Fund
3.4.2 The Group of Ministers (GoM) in the meeting held on 12th April, 2005, had conceptualized
that ‘convergence of National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) and Calamity Relief Fund (CRF)
with the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)
respectively, will ensue, after the law is enacted, over a period of time.
3.4.3 In an inter-ministerial meetipg taken by Secretary(BM) MHA, the MOF expressed the view
that time is not ripe for constituting the NDRF, as the Schemes of CRF/NCCF existing for the

20
same purpose are working satisfactorily. Further, Schemes of CRF and NCCF have been fonnulated
based on the recommendations of the successive Finance Commissions constituted under the
provisions of the Constitution of India, for the purpose of deciding on the devolution of finances
from the Central Government to the State Governments. The Ministry of Finance further expressed
the views that discontinuing the existing Schemes of NCCF/CRF and merging them with NDRF/
SDRF without the recommendation from the Finance Commission will adversely affect the federal
principles relating to financial devolution. Therefore, the Ministry of Finance suggested that these
issues may be referred to the Thirteenth Finance Commission for its consideration and
recommendations, as and when it is constituted.
3.4.4 After detailed deliberations the Inter-Ministerial meeting observed that more than a year has
lapsed since enactment of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and therefore it may not be
appropriate to say that time is not ripe for constituting the NDRF as envisaged in the Act and a
note for Cabinet may be prepared to give effect to the Provisions of DM Act and in pursuance
of the decision of GOM regarding creation of NDRF. Accordingly, a draft Cabinet Note, after the
approval of Hon’ble Home Minister, has been circulated to the concerned Central Ministries/
Departments for Inter-Ministerial consultations. After the receipt of comments/views from them,
the note will be submitted to the Cabinet for consideration.
II. National Disaster Mitigation Fund
3.4.5 The modalities for creation of National Disaster Mitigation Fund have been discussed in an
inter-ministerial meeting taken by Secretary (BM), MHA with the Ministry of Finance, the National
Disaster Management Authority and Planning Commission. Accordingly, a proposal for creating the
Fund is being processed for seeking approval of the competent authority.
Further Recommendation
3.4.6 It is unfortunate that the constitution of NDRF is still at consultation stage. The
Government should take early action in the matter and see that NDRF is in place
converging CRF/NCCF.
3.4.7 The Committee notes that a provision for creation of National Disaster Mitigation
Fund was made way lack in DM Act, 2005. Undue delay has taken place in discussion of
MHA with the Ministry of Finance, the National Disaster Management Authority and
Planning Commission. The Committee recommends that the process of creating the fund
may be completed at the earliest.

3.5 India-Bangladesh Border Fencing Work
3.5.1 The Committee is very much concerned about the problems being faced by the people
residing at the Border areas. It is a fact that there are properties of the border people where
agricultural activities are carried out and in some areas, people are also residing in this 150-yard
area. The Committee is anguished to note that people face lot of problems under the current
dispensation and no solution has been found so far for this problem. The Committee recommends
that the Government may hold discussion with Bangladesh in consultation with the Ministry of
External Affairs for a settlement of the problem. In consultation with all concerned, the fencing
may be taken nearer to the border instead of 150 yards away from  the border. In case it is not
possible, the Government may buy the land within this ISO-yard of the Border so that the people
who have properties within this area may not face problems any more. The Ministry of Home
Affairs may hold discussions with all concerned, including the Ministry of External Affairs and find
a permanent solution at the earliest.
(Para 13.9)

21
Action Taken replies
3.5.2 The matter has been under discussion with Bangladesh during each DG Level BSF-BDR
Talks since 2004 including the last DG Level Talks, held in March, 2007. BDR, however, did not
agree to the proposal of allowing construction of the fence within 150 yards.
3.5.3 In the Home Secretary Level Talks between India and Bangladesh held on October 27-
28, 2005, the Indian side emphasized that border fencing within zero to 150 yards of the border

3.5.4 The matter relating to buying of land falling within 150 yards has been considered by the

Further Recommendation
3.5.5 The Committee has constituted a sub-Committee to make a detailed study of the
Border fencing and Floodlighting projects. After the study is completed, the Committee will

3.6 Naxalism
3.6.1 The Committee agrees that naxal threat is a big menace for any industry, including the
private sector. The issue needs to be examined to see that private sector industries are also
protected in the naxal-affected areas. The Ministry of Home Affairs may examine the matter in
consultation with all concerned and take an early decision.
(Para 14.8)
Action Taken
3.6.2 Law and order is a State subject. The Central Government supplements and coordinates the
efforts and resources of the State Governments to enable them to combat the Naxal problem. 33
Battalions of Central Para Military Forces (CPMFs) have been deployed for assisting the State
Police forces in the Naxal affected States. 29 India Reserve Battalions have been sanctioned.
3.6.3 The security aspects in respect of the Private Sector industries have to be seen in the
context of the overall law and order situation. Some Private Sector industries also make their own
arrangements for security by employing their own security personnel or by engaging personnel
from private security agencies. The State/local police also responds to their problems as part of
its normal duties.
3.6.4 Security related issues are also being discussed regularly during interactions with the State
Governments, in the context of threats from/activities of terrorist/extremist elements, and action as
required to strengthen the arrangements in specific vulnerable areas is being taken on a continuing
basis.

22
Further Recommendation
3.6.5 Naxalism is no longer the problem of one State. As part of holistic approach, the
Private Sector also needs to be protected. The economic development of naxal affected areas
can happen only if Private Sector also contributes to this. Therefore, there is need for
making a policy for protecting industries including Private Sector.

3.8 Acquiring of weapons by Sportspersons
3.8.1 The Committee feels that use of advanced and imported weapons is essential for shooters
who participate in National and International championships. To enable the shooters to excel in
international events, it is necessary for the Government to allow them to import advanced weapons.
The Government may consider all the aspects relating to permission for acquiring of imported
weapons by the shooters and take an early decision in the matter. The Committee also suggested
that the sportspersons, so permitted to acquire imported weapons, may also be permitted to dispose
them of after every three years as the use of the weapons may involve wear and tear and
technological changes may make it obsolete.
(Para 19.3)
Action Taken
3.8.2 To enable the shooters to excel in international events, the Government has already allowed

23
“Renowned Shooters” to import the advanced weapons ( i.e. four per event subject to a maximum
of ten).
3.8.3 W ith a view to enable a larger number of shooters to have an opportunity to import
sophisticated weapons for practice at private ranges etc. and to come upto international level of
shooting sports, the Government has decided to enlarge the definition of “Renowned Shooter” as
follows :—
“Renowned Shooter” means a person who has participated in a National Shooting
Championship in an open Men’ s Event or open Women’ s Event or open Civilian’s Event
whether through Qualifying Tournament or Wild Card Entry and has attained the Minimum
Qualifying Score prescribed by the National Rifle Association of India.’’
3.8.4 The matter relating to sale of imported weapons by renowned shooters after three years has
also been considered and it has been decided that “Renowned Shooters” who maintain their status
of “Renowned Shooter” for three consecutive years, may be allowed to sell their imported weapons
after three years from the date of acquisition. Other “Renowned Shooters” can sell their outdated
weapons after 5 years from the date of acquisition.
Further Recommendation
3.8.5 It has been brought to the notice of the Committee by one of its member that the
following conditions imposed by the Ministry make disposal of weapons by renowned shooter
difficult:—
(a) Before allowing disposal of weapons by the renowned shooters, the condition of
the weapons may be assessed by a 3-member committee proposed to be
constituted under the Chairmanship of the Executive Director (Teams), Sports
Authority of India, with a representative each from NRAI and the National
Coach of Shooting as other members and disposal will be allowed only on the
recommendation of this committee.
(b) While disposing of such weapons, it would be ensured that these are being sold
to other upcoming shooters only subject to production of certificate to this effect
from the concerned State Association. A promising shooter would be one who
would have finished among the first three in the preceding State level
championships. After disposal, intimation to this effect will be given by the
renowned shooter to the NRAI, the Sports Authority of India and the Ministry
of Youth Affairs and Sports.
3.8.6 The Ministry, however, did not bring the above conditions to the notice of the
Committee.
3.8.7 The Committee is of the considered view that the above mentioned conditions would
create problems in the smooth disposal of outdated weapons by renowned shooters. The
meeting of the three member committee to decide disposal of weapons may not be held for
months together and the players would have no option but to wait for the outcome of the
decision of the Committee which may affect his practice/profession. Moreover, fulfilling the
condition of disposal of weapons only to promising shooters who have finished among the
first three in the preceding State level championship, would be a herculean task for the
seller shooter. The shooters who finished first three may no longer be interested in buying
outdated weapons. The Committee therefore recommends that Government may remove the
conditions of the endorsement by the three member Committee and instead straightway
allow sale of weapon by a renowned shooter to any shooter registered with Rifle Clubs/
District/State/National Rifle Association.

Besides, the Ministry is also likely to take up Phase-III of the fencing work. The Committee
strongly recommends that the physical and financial targets may be achieved well in time and
Phase-II may be completed at the earliest so that Phase-III may be commenced as soon as
possible.
(Para 13.7)
Action Taken
4.3.2 The fencing in 2429 Km. sanctioned in Phase-II, was targeted to be completed by
March, 2007. However, 1652 km. fencing has been completed by July, 2007. Fencing in remaining
stretches could not be undertaken on account of riverine segments of the border, problematic
sections; due to presence of habitation within 150 yards of international border and objections
raised by Bangladesh Rifles for construction of fence (297 kms.) and dense forest stretches in
Mizoram State. Delay in land acquisition process and other constraints have also contributed to the
non-completion of fencing (165 kms.).
4.3.3 B order fencing in Mizoram started in the year 2005. 90 km. fencing has been completed
in Mizoram till July, 2007. The balance length i.e. 310 km. is scheduled to be completed in
2008-09.
4.3.4 The feasible stretches of Phase II are envisaged to be completed by March, 2009 and a
proposal to this effect has been approved in the 16th Meeting of High Level Empowered Committee
(HLEC) held on 26th June, 2007. A Cabinet note to this effect is being prepared.
4.3.5 The financial allocation made for fencing works for Indo-Bangladesh Border during the last
three years and expenditure made is as follows:—
(Amt. Rs. in cr.)
Year Fund Released Expenditure
2004-05 270.47 270.47
2005-06 439.40 439.40
2006-07 424.00 424.00
4.3.6 Commencement of Phase III i.e. replacement of Phase I fencing, is not linked with Phase
II works and it is being taken up separately.

27
Recommendation
4.4 Modernisation of Prison Administration
4.4.1 The Committee is presently examining the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment)
Bill, 2006. One of the provisions in the Bill seeks to amend Section 167 of the Code for allowing
video conferencing between the jail and the Court for trial of an accused to avoid transportation
of the accused to the Court. To make this provision workable it is essential to modernize the jails,
especially enabling those with IT facilities, computers and all related equipments. Most of the jails
in the country do not have this facility at present. In case, the above mentioned amendment is
enacted, it would practically be of no use unless the required infrastructure is available in the jails.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that creation of infrastructure in the jails for enabling video
linkages between the jails and the courts, may be made part of the scheme of Modernization of
Prisons and if necessary a separate allocation may be made for that purpose.
(Para 16.7)
Action Taken replies
4.4.2 The Ministry of Home Affairs have noted the recommendation of the Committee for creating
infrastructure in the jails for enabling video linkage between the jails and in the Courts. The State
Governments have been requested to send their proposals for video conferencing and
computerization. A technical group is being constituted to study the facilities of video conferencing
set up in States like Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra etc. so as to evolve parameters for
introducing video conferencing/computerization in a most cost effective manner and to also evaluate
the proposals received from States in this regard. Once the estimates have been worked out and
finalized, MHA will approach the Finance Ministry/Cabinet for a higher allocation during the current
phase for implementation of the aforesaid components.
Committee’s Observation
4.4.3 The Committee has appointed a sub-committee to make a detailed study of schemes
relating to Modernisation of Prison Administration. After the study is complete, the
Committee will present a separate report thereon.
Recommendation
4.5 Housing for Central Police Forces (CPF) personnel
4.5.1 The Committee is constrained to note that the Plan Allocation approved by the Planning
Commission for the Tenth Five Year Plan of Rs.1037.50 crore was reduced to Rs.729 crore. The
originally projected expenditure for the Tenth Plan by the Ministry was Rs.l0,000 crore. The
Committee desires that the Planning Commission may make a realistic assessment of the
requirement of the scheme and make allocations accordingly. Had the projected expenditure of
Rs.2,000 crore under Plan and Non-Plan been spent during the Tenth Plan, the satisfaction level
of Twenty Five per cent would have been achieved. Due to reduction in allocation, that satisfaction
level may have gone down drastically. The Committee desires that at least 20% satisfaction level
in all the States needs to be achieved for which necessary allocation may be made. The Committee
also recommends that the Government may commission a review of the implementation of the
scheme with a view to critically analyze its implementation.
(Para 17.3)
Action Taken
4.5.2 A proposal for achieving the desired housing satisfaction level of about 21% in the Central
Para-military Forces (CPFs) in the Eleventh Plan period has been mooted, for which a requirement

28
of Rs.6584.10 crore during the Eleventh Plan has been projected before the Planning Commission.
The Planning Commission has been apprised about the comments of the Standing Committee.
Further detailed discussions have been held with Planning Commission at the level of Home
Secretary and the matter is being pursued with them.
Recommendation
4.6 Housing for Delhi Police Personnel
4.6.1 The Committee is unhappy to note that none of the housing projects on hand of the Delhi
Police, has taken off so far. The project at Dwarka could not commence due to increase in plinth
area/covered area as per requirement of Delhi Urban Arts Commission. The Committee feels that
the outstanding issues should have been sorted out before the project was approved. Now that the
tenders have already been invited for starting the construction work, the Committee recommends
that the physical targets may be adhered to.
(Para 17.7)
Action Taken
4.6.2 A provision of Rs.26.78 crore was made in the year 2001 for construction of 342 houses
in Dwarka. The work was entrusted to RITES which prepared the building plan for the residential
quarters by 2004. The same were submitted to DDA for approval. After due scrutiny DDA referred
the building drawings to Delhi Urban Arts Commission in December, 2005. Approvals of the
Airports Authority of India and the Chief Fire Officer, Delhi were also obtained in the meanwhile.
Tenders were invited but only one firm qualifIed in the technical scrutiny since the bid amount was
more than the estimated cost of the project (R.E. Rs.48.05 crore), it was re-tendered. Now the
process of re-tendering is on.
4.6.3 The time taken in starting of the project is not attributable only to the increase in plinth area
as required by the Delhi Urban Arts Commission. A number of factors have contributed such as
time required for preparation of drawings by RITES, time taken for scrutiny by DDA and the Delhi
Urban Arts Commission and finally the non-availability of competitive bids for undertaking the
work.
4.6.4 The revised administrative and expenditure sanction for the construction of work of above
project has been obtained. The plans of the above project have been got approved from Local
Bodies. The Notice inviting tender for the execution of above work has been published in the
leading newspapers on 31.5.2007.
4.6.5 T echnical Bid has been evaluated by the Tender Committee and two reputed firms have
quoted. The financial bid has been opened and the bids are being examined.
4.6.6 In accordance with the observation of the Standing Committee, a mechanism would be put
in place to ensure close monitoring of progress so as to adhere to the physical targets as opined
by the Hon’ble Committee.
Further Recommendation
4.6.7 The Committee has appointed a sub-committee to make a detailed study of Housing
Schemes for Delhi Police Personnel and Central Police Forces. After the study is complete,
the Committee will present a separate report thereon.
Recommendation
4.7 Demand No.94 – Andaman and Nicobar Islands
4.7.1 The Committee also understands that the Island Administration has a proposal of

29
procurement of two fixed wing aircrafts and two helicopters which is held up in Ministry of Civil
Aviation. The Ministry of Civil Aviation may clear the proposal at the earliest. The Ministry of
Home Affairs may also consult the Ministry of Civil Aviation for an early clearance of the proposal.
(Para 20.19)
Action Taken
4.7.2 Ministry of Civil Aviation has completed the Techno-Economic Evaluation of the proposal
and M/s Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. has been authorized to procure two 11-15 seaters helicopters
and two fixed wing aircrafts (one each of 9-10 seater and 15-19 seater) on behalf of A&N
Administration. M/s Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd. has finalized EFC Memo for procurement of fixed
wing aircraft and the same has been sent to UT Administration for vetting. EFC Memo for
helicopters is still under preparation.
Further Recommendation
4.7.3 The Committee would like to be informed of the final outcome of the efforts made.
Recommendation
4.8 Demand No. 96–Dadra and Nagar Haveli; and
Demand No. 97–Daman and Diu
4.8.1 The Committee is constrained to note that both the Union Territories of Daman and Diu and
Dadra and Nagar Haveli have been getting very less grant as compared to the projections made by
them. In fact, Dadra and Nagar Haveli has been given about one-third of the projected amount
whereas Daman and Diu has been less than 50 per cent of the projected amount. With this
reduction in the allocations, the activities proposed to be taken up by the Union Territories would
be considerably affected. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the allocations for
both the Union Territories may be increased appropriately at RE level. The Ministry of Home Affairs
may also hold discussions with the Planning Commission about the necessity of the projects to be
taken up by the Union Territories. The Committee also recommends that the priority areas of
activities proposed to be taken up during 2007-08 may be completed as per the targets fixed.
Energy sector is an important area in which both the Union Territories proposed to set up new
sub-stations. Dadra and Nagar Haveli also proposed to augment the capacity of a sub-station and
Daman and Diu proposes to convert overhead lines to underground lines. These activities may be
undertaken on a priority basis and completed as per the targets fixed.
(Para 23.6)
Action Taken replies
4.8.2 The Union Territory Administration of Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli have
taken up the matter with the Planning Commission to augment the Plan allocation to Rs.190 crore
and Rs.232 crore, respectively, at RE 2007-08 stage. Ministry of Home Affairs has also requested
Planning Commission in July, 2007 to consider the proposal of these UTs favourably. MHA has also
taken up with Planning Commission for revival of the practice of consultation/discussions with the
two UT Adminsitrations for finalizing their Annual Plan Outlays. Planning Commission has agreed
to revive the practice from next Annual Plan.
4.8.3 Necessary actions are being expedited to complete activities proposed to be taken up during
2007-08 as per the targets fixed.
Further Recommendation
4.8.4 The Committee would like to be informed the present status of various activities
taken up in 2007-08 along with the targets and achievements.

Civic Action Programme of Border Guarding Forces

(Para 1.1.5)

The Committee notes that the Ministry of Home Affairs has forwarded the
"Comprehensive Composite Proposal" to the Planning Commission for technology
upgradation in the functioning of police at all level through a project called CIP A-crime
registration, investigation, and prosecution modules to be linked through a broadband/
CDMA/VSAT network. The Committee desires that the Planning Commission may clear the

The Committee has appointed a sub-Committee to make a detailed study of the
scheme. After the study is completed by the sub-Committee a separate and detailed report

The Committee has appointed a sub-Committee to make a detailed study of the
scheme. After the study is completed by the sub-Committee a separate and detailed report
would be presented by the Committee to the Parliament. (Para 1.8.3)
Recommendation
Demand No.94–Andaman & Nicobar Islands
The Committee desirers that the 50 sites identified for development may be taken
up immediately. Development of the sites would give employment opportunities to a large
number of people in the area. (Para 1.10.7)
Relief and rehabilitation measures for J&K migrants
The Committee has appointed a sub-Committee to make a detailed study on the
select and Rehabilitation measures for J&K Migrants. After the study is completed, the

Coastal Security Scheme
The Committee is constrained to note that even though the scheme was approved in
2005 for implementation in five years several proposals are still in approval stage. The

30

31
National Disaster Management Authority
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should expediously
consider the Draft National Policy on Disaster Management as prepared by the National
Disaster Management Authority and finalize the policy at the earliest. The country can not
wait for a disaster to happen before the policy is finalized. (Para 3.3.3)
National Disaster Management Authority
It is unfortunate that the constitution of NDRF is still at consultation stage. The
Government should take early action in the matter and see that NDRF is in place
converging CRF/NCCF. (Para 3.4.6)
The Committee notes that a provision for creation of National Disaster Mitigation
Fund was made way lack in DM Act, 2005. Undue delay has taken place in discussion of
MHA with the Ministry of Finance, the National Disaster Management Authority and
Planning Commission. The Committee recommends that the process of creating the fund
may be completed at the earliest. (Para 3.4.7)
India-Bangladesh Border Fencing Work
The Committee has constituted a sub-Committee to make a detailed study of the
Border fencing and Floodlighting projects. After the study is completed, the Committee will
present a separate report thereon. (Para 3.5.5)
Naxalism
Naxalism is no longer the problem of one State. As part of holistic approach, the
private sector also needs to be protected. The economic development of naxal affected areas
can happen only if private sector also contributes to this. Therefore, there is need for
making a policy for protecting industries including private sector. (Para 3.6.5)
Housing for Delhi Police Personnel
The Committee was appointed a sub-Committee to make a detailed study of the
Housing for CPMF and Delhi Police. After the study is completed by the sub-Committee, the
Committee will present its detailed report thereon. (Para 3.7.5)
Acquiring of weapons by sportspersons
It has been brought to the notice of the Committee by one of its member that the
following conditions imposed by the Ministry make disposal of weapons by renowned shooter
difficult:—
(a) Before allowing disposal of weapons by the renowned shooters, the condition of
the weapons may be assessed by a 3-member committee proposed to be
constituted under the Chairmanship of the Executive Director (Teams), Sports
Authority of India, with a representative each from NRAI and the National
Coach of Shooting as other members and disposal will be allowed only on the
recommendation of this committee.
(b) While disposing of such weapons, it would be ensured that these are being sold
to other upcoming shooters only subject to production of certificate to this effect
from the concerned State Association. A promising shooter would be one who
would have finished among the first three in the preceding State level
championships. After disposal, intimation to this effect will be given by the
renowned shooter to the NRAI, the Sports Authority of India and the Ministry
of Youth Affairs and Sports. (Para 3.8.5)

32
The Ministry, however, did not bring the above conditions to the notice of the
Committee. (Para 3.8.6)
The Committee is of the considered view that the above mentioned conditions would
create problems in the smooth disposal of outdated weapons by renowned shooters. The
meeting of the three member committee to decide disposal of weapons may not be held for
months together and the players would have no option but to wait for the outcome of the
decision of the committee which may affect his practice/profession. Moreover, fulfilling the
condition of disposal of weapons only to promising shooters who have finished among the
first three in the preceding State level championship, would be a herculean task for the
seller shooter. The shooters who finished first three may no longer be interested in buying
outdated weapons. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government may remove
the conditions of the endorsement by the three member committee and instead straightway
allow sale of weapon by a renowned shooter to any shooter registered with Rifle Clubs/
District/State/National Rifle Association. (Para 3.8.7)

PREFACE
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Thirty First Report on Action Taken by Government on the
recommendations/observations contained in the One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Report on
Demands for Grants (2007-08) of the Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region.
2. The One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok
Sabha on 8 May, 2007.
3. The Ministry of DoNER furnished the Action Taken Replies on the One Hundred and
Twenty Seventh Report of the Committee. The Minister for Development of North Eastern Region
laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha the status of implementation of the recommendations contained
in the said Report of the Committee, in pursuant to the Chairman, Rajya Sabha’s Direction dated
24th September, 2004, like the previous year, the Committee is again constrained to observe
that both these documents are identical, word-by-word. If the statement of the Minister laid
after nearly four months of the Action Taken Replies sent by the Ministry to the
Secretariat, is a mere reproduction of the ATR, it would defeat the spirit underlying the
Chairman’s Direction.
4. The Committee considered the draft Report and adopted the same at its meeting held on
11th April, 2008.
5. The Recommendations/Observations of the Committee are printed in bold letters.
SUSHMA SWARAJ

1
REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Twenty Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs on Demands for Grants (2007-08). The Report was presented to/laid on the Table of Rajya
Sabha and Lok Sabha on the 8 May, 2007.
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I: The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the
Government: Paras: 12.8, 18.3, 20.1, 23.2, 24.2, 25.1;
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendation as
mentioned in Chapter–I of the Report.
Chapter II: The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire
to pursue in view of the Government’s replies: – Para: 13.3, 13.4, 16.1;
In respect of this recommendation the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanation advanced by the Ministry and, therefore, does not want to pursue it further.
Chapter III: The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee
has not accepted the replies of the Ministry: Paras: 12.7, 14.6, 15.4, 19.6, 21.4, 22.6,
22.7; 27.1
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementations of recommendations
contained in Chapter–III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanation in respect
of these recommendations.
Chapter–IV: The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of
the Government have not been received: 14.5, 17.3, 24.1, 26.5
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter–IV , the Ministry has either furnished the
interim replies or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee desires that the
Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respect of the recommendations categorized in
Chapter–IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the
Committee.
3. The details of the ATR have been discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.

2
CHAPTER–I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
RECOMMENDATION
1.1 SURRENDER OF LARGE SUM OF MONEY
1.1.1 The Committee expresses its concern over the surrender of large sums of money by
different Ministries, which ultimately go into NLCPR. Even the Ministries of social sector
are also not able to spend 10 per cent of their budget in the Region. If the national norms
for any particular programme are found to be unsuitable for the North-Eastern Region, the
Ministry concerned should relax the norms according to the conditions of the North-Eastern
States so that the allocation made is spent in the year in which it was allocated.
(Para 12.8)
Action Taken

1.6 HEALTH SYSTEM
1.6.1 Considering the different demography, topography and the needs of the region,
national norms of MCI for setting up medical colleges cannot be applied there. The
Committee feels that the norms should not come in the way of providing health
infrastructure in the NE Region. The Committee recommends that the norms may be

4
revised for NER. Steps may also be taken to start medical colleges in every State as
recommended by the Committee earlier.
(Para 25.1)
Action Taken
1.6.2 According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, following decisions have been
taken to facilitate setting up of new medical colleges in the Region:
(i) In the past new medical colleges in the country were permitted to utilize the facilities of
other Government/district hospitals for a period of three years from the date of grant of permission
by the Central Government for their establishment, mainly for utilizalion of ciinical material for
teaching purpose. It was stipulated therein that beds of these Government hospitals should be under
the total administrative control of the concerned college and the hospital should be situated within
5 kms. from the medical college. In view of the difficulties being experienced by medical colleges
located in north-eastern, hilly and tribal areas, it has now been decided that the new medical
colleges may be permitted to utilize the facilities of other Government/district hospitals for clinical
material for teaching purpose upto ten years from the date of permission for establishment of
college subject to the condition that beds of these Govt. owned hospitals must be clearly earmarked
for utilization by teaching faculty and further that the academic and clinical control of the patients
must be with the teaching faculty of the medical colleges and the hospital is situated within a
maximum distance of 10 km. from the medical college. The college authorities are, however,
required to ensure that the infrastructure and other facilities in district/Government hospitals being
so utilized are developed as per MCI Regulations.
(ii) The second issue relates to deficiency in faculty of private medical colleges. The Medical
Council of India has allowed a maximum upto 5% deficiency in faculty as condonable because
delay takes place in filling up of the vacancies and some times suitable candidates are not available.
Also the Council has been allowing renewal/recognition of Government Colleges with 10 per cent
faculty deficiency, if the State Government gives assurance/commitment to fill up vacant faculty
positions within a given time. In case of medical colleges established in North Eastern States, hilly
and tribal areas, which are unable to draw maximum number of faculty because of various
conditions, it has been decided that the MCI may hereafter condone 15 per cent deficiency of
faculty at the time of recognition of the institution with the stipulation that the institution would
fill up vacant faculty positions within a given period of three more years and make itself self-
sufficient in every respect.
(iii) The third issue is that indoor bed occupancy in hospitals attached to medical colleges in
North Eastern States, hilly and tribal areas is not upto the stipulated percentage of 80 per cent as
is required as per MCI norms. Considering the hilly and difficult terrain and sparse population in
those areas, MCI may even allow and consider 65 per cent bed occupancy in hospitals attached
to the private medical college in such areas and to encourage private-public partnership while
considering recognition of colleges located in these areas.

of Asian Development Bank (ADB) is an important project for the overall growth of trade
and industry in the North-Eastern States. The Draft Report submitted by the ADB
Consultants may be examined at the earliest and a final decision may be taken soon to
make the project functional. The Committee also learned that the North-Eastern States are
asking for more land custom stations and development of infrastructure in the existing
stations. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may examine these issues and take
up with the concerned Ministries and take an early decision. Development of infrastructure
at the custom stations is very essential because without proper infrastructure, the custom
stations will not be successful. The Ministry of DoNER may consider this aspect and take
up the infrastructure development for custom stations on a priority basis with separate
allocation, if required.
(Para 26.5)
Action Taken
4.4.2 As per Min istry of Commerce, the infrastructure for the International Trade Promotion
Centre at Guwahati is in place. The centre is likely to be commissioned shortly. Another Centre
in the name of “North Eastern Agri-Expo Centre” at Dimapur, Nagaland sanctioned, under NLCPR
scheme of Ministry of DONER, for establishment.
4.4.3 Ministry of DONER through Technical Assistance (TA) of Asian Development Bank (ADB)
seeks to develop a project for the North Eastern States Trade and Investment Creative Initiative
(NES-TICI) so as to build on the locational advantage of the NER States with international borders
with five countries. Draft study report prepared through ADB assistance was discussed with the
NE States and other stakeholders in a Regional Workshop held at Guwahati. It was circulated to
all the stakeholders and the consultations are on to finalise the report taking into consideration
the new North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP) 2007 launched from
1st April, 2007.

15
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS OF THE COMMITTEE—
AT A GLANCE
NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
The Committee reiterates its recommends that government may consider the matter
again and take out some more Ministries from the list of exempted Ministries.
(Para 3.1.3)
UNDUE DELAY IN PILOT AND AIRHOSTESS TRAINING
The Committee expresses its disquiet over the continuing delay in identifying the
institute for pilot and airhostess training. The Committee recommends that the institutes
may be selected immediately so that training may start without further delay.
(Para 3.2.3)
EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECTS
The Committee apprehends that both the projects, viz.  North Eastern Urban
Development Project (NEUDP) and Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM) may be delayed in the process of approval and transfer. The Committee desires
that these projects should start without any further delay. (Para 3.3.4)
CIVIL A VIATION
The Committee reiterates its observation that inter and intra air connectivity of NER
would prove a sine qua non  for the all round development of North Eastern Region, be it
a tourist destiny or economic development or inducement investment. The Committee,
therefore, strongly, recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should not confine itself
merely to forwarding the development projects from one Ministry to the other but, being
the territorial Ministry endowed with role and responsibility of developing the North-Eastern
Region, should play pro-active and result-oriented role in pursuing continuously so far as
the inception and implementation of the proposal/ undertaken projects are concerned viz.
improvement of inter and intra region air services; setting up of Greenfield airports at
Kohima, Itanagar, Gangtok and for upgradation of airports of Pasight and Tezu in Arunachal
Pradesh, Baljek in West Goro Hills, Meghalaya and Kamalpur and Kailashah in Tripura.
These projects should be completed within the stipulated time frame and should not incur
time and cost overruns. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER
should take adequate follow up action with the Ministry of Civil Aviation for harnessing the
vast pool of trained pilots and technical staff of IAF by inducting them on permanent
absorption basis. (Para 3.4.7)
PROMOTION OF INDUSTRIES
The Committee feels that the Ministry of DoNER should not ony pro-actively liase
and take follow-up initiatives/action with the Department of IPP, (Government of India) and
NEDFI (North Eastern Development Finance Corporation) but should also interact with the
Ministry of Small Micro and Medium Enterprises for promoting micro, small and medium
enterprises in the NE, region. (Para 3.5.3)
15

16
AGRICULTURE SECTOR
The Committee is constrained t6 note that the Ministry of Agriculture is not able to
spend their entire allocation in the NER. The Ministry of Agriculture must ensure that the
allocated budget is spent. (Para 3.6.5)
PROBLEMS AND PROSPECTS OF AGRICULTURAL SECTOR
The Committee desires that pattas may be issued to the small tea growers at the
earliest. The Committee also desires that the projects reports may be obtained from state
governments on Rubber Plantations and the Task Force may finalize its recommendations
at the earliest. (Para 3.7.3)
SPECIAL INITIATIVES
The Committee desires that the Cabinet Secretariat may make the provision in the
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 as the earliest, that the line
Ministries would consult the Ministry of DoNER before finalizing any scheme to be
implemented in North East. (Para 3.8.3)

PREFACE
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs having been authorised by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Thirty second Report on Demands for Grants (2008-09) relating to
the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
2. While examining Demands for Grants every year, it has been the practice in this Committee
to take up one subject/issue for special focus. It had earlier taken up “Disaster Management”,
“Delhi Police and its functioning” and “Union Territories without Legislature” focused study during
2005-06, 2006-07 and 2007-08, respectively. In the current year, the Committee had decided to
highlight “Naxalism” in its report. To facilitate in-depth examination of the subject by the

it. However, keeping in view the wide ranging implications of the subject, the Committee decided
to make a detailed study of the subject and present a separate report after taking into account the
views of the affected State Governments.
3. The Committee held in all three sittings to complete the examination of Demands for Grants
of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Committee heard the Home Secretary on Demands for Grants

REPORT
CHAPTER-I
OVERVIEW
Maintenance of internal security, management of para-military forces, border management,
Centre-State relations, administration of Union Territories, disaster management are the major
responsibilities of the Ministry of Home Affairs. In addition, the Ministry also has the following
broad responsibilities:
(i) Issue of Notification in respect of Appointment of President/Vice-President, Prime
Minister and Members of the Union Council of Ministers;
(ii) Appointment of Governors and Lt. Governors;
(iii) Regulation of Pay and Allowances of the Ministers;
(iv) Carrying out Census in India once every ten years;
(v) Implementation of the Provisions of the Official Language Act, 1963;
(vi) Maintenance of Communal Harmony and Promotion of National Integration;
(vii) Co-ordination of Policy relating to Human Rights;
(viii) Providing Relief and Rehabilitation to Refugees/Displaced Persons;
(ix) Regulation of Entry of Foreigners into India;
(x) Grant of Pension and Other Benefits to Freedom Fighters; and
(xi) Prevention and Combat of Drug Abuse and Drug Trafficking.
2. To discharge the above responsibilities, the Ministry has been divided into following six
constituent Departments:
(i) Department of Internal Security;
(ii) Department of States;
(iii) Department of Home;
(iv) Department of Jammu and Kashmir (J and K) Affairs;
(v) Department of Border Management; and
(vi) Department of Official Language.
2.1 The Department of Internal Security deals with Indian Police Service, Central Police
Forces, internal security and law and order, insurgency, terrorism, naxalism, activities of inimical
foreign agencies, rehabilitation, grant of visa and other immigration matters, security clearances, etc.
2.2 Department of States deals with Centre-State relations, Inter-State relations, administration
of Union Territories, freedom fighters’ pension, human rights, prison reforms, police reforms, etc.
2.3 Department of Home deals with notification of assumption of office by the President and
Vice-President, notification of appointment/resignation of the Prime Minister, Ministers, Governors,
nomination to Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha, census of population, registration of births and deaths, etc.

2
2.4 Department of Jammu and Kashmir Affairs deals with the constitutional provisions in
respect of the State of Jammu and Kashmir and all other matters relating to the State, excluding
those with which the Ministry of External Affairs is concerned.
2.5 Department of Border Management deals with management of international borders
including coastal borders, strengthening of border guarding and creation of related infrastructure,
border areas development, etc.
2.6 Department of Official Language is concerned with the implementation of the provisions
of the Constitution relating to official languages and the provisions of the Official Language
Act, 1963.
3. The Ministry is under the overall charge of the Minister of Home Affairs assisted by three
Ministers of State. All Departments of the Ministry except the Department of Official Language are
interlinked and are headed by the Home Secretary who is assisted by Secretary (Border
Management), two Special Secretaries, three Additional Secretaries and nineteen Joint Secretaries.
The Department of Official Language has a separate Secretary and functions independently. The
Ministry is further divided into eighteen divisions for administrative purposes and is concerned with
the tasks mentioned below for each division:-
(i) Centre State Division
The Division deals with Central-State relations, including working of the Constitutional
provisions governing such relations; appointment of Governors; creation of new
States; nominations to Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha; Inter-State boundary disputes; over-
seeing the crime situation in States; imposition of President’s Rule; etc.
(ii) Internal Security Division
The Division deals with matters relating to internal security, including anti-national and
subversive activities of various groups/extremist organizations; policy and operational
issues on terrorism; Narcotics Control Bureau; National Security Act; etc.
(iii) Police Division
The Division functions as the cadre controlling authority of IPS officers and also
deals with all matters relating to Central Police Forces, including their deployment.
(iv) Union Territories Division
The Division deals with all legislative and constitutional matters relating to Union
Territories including Delhi and Puducherry. It also functions as the cadre controlling
authority of Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territories (AGMUT) Cadre
of IAS/IPS as also Delhi-Andaman Nicobar Islands Civil Service (DANICS)/Delhi-
Andaman Nicobar Islands Police Service (DANIPS). It is also responsible for
overseeing the crime and law and order situation in UTs.
(v) North-Eastern Division
The Division deals with the law and order situation in North-Eastern States, including
matters relating to insurgency and talks with various extremist groups operating in
that region.
(vi) Jammu and Kashmir Division
The Division deals with the Constitutional matters including Article 370 and general
policy matters in respect of J and K and terrorism/militancy in that State; it is also
responsible for implementation of the PM’s Package for J and K.
(vii) Foreigners Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to visa, Protected Area Permit/Restricted

3
Area Permit regime, immigration, citizenship, overseas citizenship of India, acceptance
of foreign contribution and hospitality.
(viii) Freedom Fighters and Rehabilitation Division
The Division frames and implements the Freedom Fighters Pension Scheme and the
schemes for rehabilitation of migrants from former West Pakistan/East Pakistan and
provision of relief to Srilankan and Tibetan refugees.
(ix) Human Rights Division
The Division deals with matters relating to the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
and also matters relating to national integration, communal harmony and Ayodhya
affairs.
(x) Disaster Management Division
This division is bifurcated into two parts: Disaster Management-I Division is
responsible for response, relief and preparedness for natural calamities and man-made
disasters (except drought and epidemics), whereas Disaster Management-II Division
is responsible for legislation, policy, capacity building, prevention, mitigation and long
term rehabilitation.
(xi) Border Management Division
This Division deals with all matters relating to management of international borders,
including coastal borders, creation of infrastructure like integrated check posts, road/
fencing and floodlighting of borders and the Border Area Development Programme.
(xii) Police Modernization Division
The Division handles all items of work relating to modernisation of State Police
Forces, provisioning/procurement of various items for modernisation of Central
Police Forces, police reforms and security of VIPs/vitals installation.
(xiii) Policy Planning Division
It deals with meetings of the SAARC Interior/Home Ministers, matters relating to
policy formulation in respect of internal security issues, international cooperation on
counter-terrorism, international covenants, bilateral assistance treaties and related
items of work.
(xiv) Finance Division
The Division is responsible for formulating, operating and controlling the budget of
the Ministry under the Integrated Finance Scheme.
(xv) Judicial Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to the legislative aspects of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the Commissions of Inquiry
Act, 1952. It also handles matters relating to the State legislations to the extent such
legislation require the assent of the President under the Constitution; political pension
to erstwhile rulers before independence and mercy petitions under Article 72 of the
Constitution.
(xvi) Administration Division
The Division is responsible for handling all administrative and vigilance matters of the
Ministry of Home Affairs, monitoring of compliance of furnishing information under
the Right to Information Act, 2005 and it also deals with matters relating to Table of
Precedence, Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards, Gallantry Awards, Jeevan Raksha
Padak, National Flag, National Anthem, State Emblem of India and Secretariat Security
Organisation.

4
(xvii) Coordination Division
The division deals with intra-Ministry coordination work, Parliamentary matters,
public grievances, publication of Annual Report of the Ministry, Record Retention
Schedule, custody of classified and non-classified records of the Ministry, Internal
Work Study, furnishing of various reports relating to employment of SCs/STs and
persons with Disabilities to Department of Personnel and Training, etc.
(xviii) Naxal Management Division
This Division was created w.e.f. October, 29, 2006 in the Ministry to effectively
tackle the naxalite menace from both security and development angles. It monitors the
naxal situation and counter-measures being taken by the affected States with the
objective of improving ground-level policing and development response as per the
location specific action plans formulated/to be formulated by the affected States and
review with the concerned Ministries/Departments to ensure optimum utilization of
funds released and proper implementation of various developmental schemes in the
naxal affected areas.
4. The Ministry has following CPOs/Organisations/Institutions functioning under its
administrative control:

OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
