1.17 HOUSING SCHEME FOR CENTRAL POLICE FORCES 
Recommendation 
1.17.1  The Committee observes that just a little more than 15% of the force personnel entitled to 
family accommodation, are able to avail the facility. Force personnel, who remain deployed at 
international borders as well as in violence infested regions, are engaged in grappling with militancy 
and insurgency throughout the year. They do not even have the mental comfort of their families having 
proper accommodation, medical facilities etc., while they are away from home. (Para 7.17.1 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.17.2  To address this issue of deficient accommodation in force personnel, a Mega Housing Project 
has been launched to construct houses across the co untry wherever land is available. The project is 
being taken up on Public Private Partnership basis on annuity mode. It is proposed to construct 
approximately 66,000 houses at approximately 250 sites, through the project. At the first instance, 
RFQ has been issued for the pilot project consisting of 5 clusters/30 sites, for construction of 13,026 
houses. Evaluation of the applications received has also been completed. In the second lot 
approximately 20, 000 houses are proposed to be built in 10 clusters / 63 sites. It is expected- that 
when completed, this project will meet the deficiency in accommodation for CPMFs satisfactorily. 
Medical facilities :-
 
1.17.3  For improvement of health care and extent of medical cover to the force personnel, the 
medical set up in CPMFs has been restructured in 2004 which provides better career prospects to 
Medical Officers so as to make it more attractive. The restructuring also provides for pooling of 
facilities for all CPMF personnel as Composite Hospital irrespective of force affiliation, upgradation 
of infrastructure and equipment and introduction of specialist treatment through upgradation/sanction 
of 6 Nos. 100-bed and 32 Nos. 50-bed composite hospitals along with one 200-bed referral hospital, 
which would be available to all CPMF personnel. 
1.17.4  In addition, uniform staffing pattern for all these composite hospitals has been approved and 
sanction for net creation of 947 Nos. of posts  has been issued. Moreover, considering the huge 
vacancy, approval has been obtained for appointment of Medical Officers (both specialist and general 
duty) on contractual basis and existing instructions relating to period of contractual appointment (1 
year) and age limit (60 years)  have been relaxed, so as to allo w contractual appointment upto 3 years 
or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. 
Further Recommendation 
1.17.5  The Committee desires that the all formalitie s concerning RFQs for first and second lots 
may be completed at the earliest. Efforts may also be made to  take up construction of the 

remaining proposed flats. The Committee appr eciates the concept of  composite hospital. 
Vigorous efforts may be made to open the hospitals expeditiously. 
Recommendation 
1.17.6  The Committee takes a serious note of the fact that the deficiency of the housing units as on 
1.4.1009 was 114634. If the new battalions, which had been approved by the Government and were 
likely to be raised by 2013-14 were also taken into account, forty thousand personnel would be further 
added. The allocations have been made as per the current requirements only. As this rate, the gap 
would keep on increasing and it would be a never ending phenomenon. The Committee agrees that the 
allocations have not kept pace with the increase in number of personnel in various Central Police 
Forces and this situation is likely to go from bad to worse. The Committee therefore recommends that 
the Government should seriously assess the financial requirements for the housing of the CPF 
personnel. The Ministry informed the Committee that due to massive housing shortage, the funds were 
inadequate and they would move for additional funds at RE stage. The Committee suggests that 
additional funds may be sought at RE 2010-11 stage.   
1.17.7  The Committee recommends that to supplement th e funds requirement, not covered by the 
Planning Commission, Ministry of Finance may be allowed to make adequate allocation from the 
‘Non-Plan’ side also so as to enable the forces to meet the housing requirements. (Para 7.17.4 ibid)  
Action Taken 
1.17.8  A Mega Housing Project for CPMF personnel under Public Private Partnership was 
announced by Finance Minister in budget speech during 2009 to meet the deficiency in CPMF 
housing. The project has been launched as a Public Private Partnership project to Annuity mode as per 
details given in para 7.17.1 above. The payment for this project will be in the form of annuity for 
which approximately an amount of Rs.43,053.02 crore will be required from 2013-14 to 2025-26. A 
request has already been made to the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for allocation of 
requisite funds. 
1.17.9  The Mega Housing Project under Public Private Partnership basis will cover the major portion 
of construction of housing. This project is under Plan Scheme for which Planning Commission and 
Ministry of Finance have already been requested to allocate funds. The housing, which will not be 
covered under the PPP project, wi ll continue under the existing Re sidential Buildi ng (Plan) and 
Residential Building (Non-Plan) scheme for which Ministry of Finance is requested to allocate funds 
in each financial year. The requirement of funds under Residential Building (Plan) and Residential 
Building (Non-Plan) will come down with the completion of the PPP project. 
Further Recommendation 
1.17.10  The Committee recommends that the matter may be regularly pursued with the 
Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for allocation of funds. 
Recommendation 

1.17.11 The Ministry proposed to launch a mega housin g project for CPFs to address problems of 
accommodation for the forces personnel on Public Private Partnership basis. The Committee desires 
that an early decision may be taken in this regard. (Para 7.17.7 ibid)

2.3 NATIONAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT 
Recommendation 
2.3.1 The Committee in its 115th Report on the Disaster Management Bill 2005 dealt with in detail 
about the mechanism to be put in place for tacklin g the natural disasters like earthquake, cyclones, 
floods. The Committee understands that there should be requisite mechanism for drawing up and 
monitoring implementation of the disaster management plans, ensuring measures for preventing and 
mitigating disaster. The NDMA may also chalk out a plan for giving training to government officials, 
on disaster management. Training on this should be made compulsory for all new recruits.(Para 3.3.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.3.2 The Disaster Management Act, 2005, envisages the creation of the National Disaster 
Management Authority (NDMA), headed by the Prime Minister, State Disaster Management 
Authorities (SDMAs) headed by the Chief Ministers, and District Disaster Management Authorities 
(DDMAs) headed by the Collector or District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner as the case may be, 
to spearhead and adopt a holistic and integrated approach to Disaster Management. There is a 
paradigm shift, from the erstwhile relief-centric response to a proactive prevention, mitigation and 
preparedness-driven approach for conserving devel opment gains and also to minimize losses of life, 
livelihood and property. 
2.3.3 NDMA under its responsibility for laying down policies, plans and guidelines for DM and 
coordinating their enforcement and implementation, has released guidelines on management of 
disasters like earthquake, floods, cyclone, biologic al, chemical (industrial), chemical (terrorism), 
nuclear and radiological emergencies, medical preparedness and mass casualty management, landslide 
and snow avalanches etc. It has also released  guidelines for National Institute of Disaster 
Management, formulation of State Disaster Management Plans and Revamping of Civil Defence and 
Fire Services. 
2.3.4 The requisite mechanism for drawing up and monitoring implementation of the disaster 
management plans has already been enshrined in the DM Act, 2005. The DM Act, 2005 envisages 
preparation of National Plan for Disaster Manageme nt for the whole of the country, State Disaster 
Management Plans and a Plan for Disaster Manage ment for every district. State plans shall be 
prepared having regard to guidelines laid down by the National Authority and district plans shall be 
prepared having regard to National Plan and State Plan. Concerned Ministries / Departments of 
Government of India have already been requested to prepare disaster mitigation plan concerning the 
disaster(s) coming under their purview. The Disaster Mitigation Plans prepared by Ministry of 
Railways, Department of Atomic Energy, Ministry of Mines and Ministry of Defence are under 
scrutiny and examination. 
2.3.5 The mandate of training and capacity building of Government officials is given to National 
Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) which works within the framework of broad polices and 

guidelines laid down by the NDMA and as new statutory body. To ensure that the Institution becomes 
a Centre of Excellence for institutionalizing training  of trainers, a comprehensive set of guidelines on 
the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) have been issued by the NDMA. 
2.3.6 The NIDM has taken up capacity development as one of its major responsibilities, along with 
training, research, documentation and development of a national level information base. It networks 
with other knowledge-based institutions and functions within the broad policies and guidelines laid 
down by the NDMA. It organizes training of trainers, Government officials and other stakeholders. 
The NIDM is developing and facilitating the implementation of the national training schedule for DM. 
It is the nodal institution for regional and international cooperation for training. NIDM has conducted 
287 programmes in past five years i.e. from 2005-06 to 2009-10 and trained 8150 persons. 
2.3.7 NIDM is also preparing the “National Human Resource and Capacity Building Plan” which 
aims at enhancing the capacity and quality of human resource available with some key government 
departments in India, mainly in the State Governments, for more efficient and effective disaster 
management in the country. 
2.3.8 NIDM is also implementing a programme for capacity building of Engineers & Architects for 
earthquake risk management. Under this programme, 266 Master Trainers (Architects), 308 Master 
Trainers in the field of Engineering, 2906 prac ticing Engineers and 1825 practicing Architects have 
been trained so far. The approach also includes according priority to training for developing 
community based DM systems for their specific needs in view of the regional diversion and multi 
hazard vulnerabilities.

2.7 COASTAL SECURITY 
Recommendation 
2.7.1 The Committee wishes to highlight the imperative need for a robust coastal security in the 
backdrop of the modalities of the 26/11 attack. The Committee recommends that the Government 
should make all efforts to ensure that comprehensive and fool-proof coastal security is put in place so 
that another 26/11 type attack may not take place. (Para 3.9.2 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.7.2 Subsequent to the Mumbai incidents on 26/1 1, the entire coastal security scenario of the 
country has been subjected to multi-level inter-mi nisterial review by the Government of India and 
several important decisions/initiatives have been taken, which are briefly outlined below :–– 
(i) The Indian Coast Guard has been additionally designated as the authority responsible for 
coastal security in territorial waters including areas to be patrolled by the Coastal Police. 
The Indian Navy is designated as the authority responsible for overall maritime security, 
which includes coastal security and offshore security. 
(ii) The Director General, Coast Guard has been designated as Commander, Coastal 
Command and will be responsible for overall coordination between Central and State 
agencies in all matters relating to coastal security. 
(iii) Ministry of Defence (MoD) has set up four Joint Operation Centres (JOC) at Mumbai, 
Visakhapatnam, Kochi and Port Blair. 
(iv) MoD is in the process of creating ‘Sagar  Prahari Bal’ for protection of coast line. 
(v) Draft Standard Operating Procedures (SoP) for coordination among various agencies has 
been circulated by Coast Guard and most of the States/UTs have given their comments. 
MoD is now finalizing the SoPs. 

(vi) Government has decided that all the fishing/non-fishing boats plying in Indian waters 
will be registered under a uniform system. The Ministry of Shipping has issued two 
notifications in June 2009, one for amending the MS (Registration of Fishing Vessels) 
Rules along with revised format for registration and another for notifying the list of 
registrars. States/UTs are taking follow-up action in this regard. 
(vii) It has been decided that all type of boats should be fitted/provided with transponders to 
facilitate vessels identification and tracking. 
  The DG, Shipping has issued the two circulars to ensure that all types of vessels 
including fishing vessels, other than fishing vessels of less than 20 mtr. category, are 
installed with AIS type B transponders. St ates/UTs are taking necessary steps for 
compliance of these circulars. 
  As for vessels of less than 20 mtr. category, a Committee under the DG, Coast 
Guard, has carried out NCNC trials of suitable tracking systems for sub-20 mtrs. boats, 
which are - (a) Satellite based; (b) AIS/ VHF based; and (c) VHF/GPS based. While the 
final deliberations for the most suitable technology or a mix of technologies are in 
progress, it has been recommended that RFID device should be installed on all the boats. 
(viii) Government has decided that all the fishermen should be issued ID cards which should 
be related to a single centralized data-base. 
  Ministry of Agriculture has, on 11th December, 2009, launched Central Sector 
Scheme on ‘Issuance of Biometric Identity cards  to coastal fishermen’ at a total cost of 
Rs.72.00 crore. A Consortium of three P ublic Sector Undertakings led by Bharat 
Electronics Limited (BEL) has been identified for the work of digitization of data, card 
production and issuance. DAHD&F has released a sum of Rs.8.00 crore to the coastal 
States/UTs for implementation of the project. An amount of Rs.25.00 crore has also been 
released to the three PSUs of the aforesaid c onsortium. This project of issuance of ID 
cards to fisherman is being funded by the RGI, MHA. 
(ix) Registrar General of India (RGI), MHA, is working a project for preparation of National 
Population Register (NPR) for the coastal population of the country, ahead of Census 
2011. Under this project, Identify (Smart) Cards would be issued to all the usual 
residents of the coastal villages, who are above 18 years of age. In the first phase, 3331 
villages on the coastline are being covered (in A&N Islands, all the villages and towns to 
be covered in Phase – I). The biographic data  collection as well as biometric capture is 
expected to be completed by the end of June, 2010. 
(x) Implementation of ongoing Coastal Security Scheme, including supply of interceptor 
boats has been expedited. Till May 2010, 125 boats have been delivered to States and 
UTs. The Coastal Security Scheme has been extended till March, 2011, with an 
additional non-recurring outlay of Rs.95 crore (approx.), by the CCS decision taken on 
June 10,2010. 
(xi) In pursuance of one of the major decision taken by the Government after 26/11, the 
coastal States/UTs have carried out vulnerability/gap analysis in consultation with Coast 
Guard to firm up their additiona l requirements for formulation of Phase-II of the Coastal 

Security. Based on the input s/proposals received from th e Coast Guard and coastal 
States/UTs, the Coastal Security Scheme (P hase-II) has been formulated and necessary 
clearances being taken.

Recommendation 
2.9.1 Organization of a sporting event like the Commonwealth Games is a major challenge for any

(Para 3.11.6 ibid)

2.9.4 Further, coordination meetings are being regularly organized by IB with the representatives

2.9.5 Delhi Police would ensure that there is no security lapse in the security arrangements for want 
of resources. Venue Commanders and Nodal Officers for the Games Venues and Games Village have 
been nominated. 
2.9.6 The Cabinet has approved Rs.370 crore for installation of integrated Security System which 
will be provided by M/s Electronics Corporation of India Ltd. (ECIL). Contract Agreement between 
the Venue Owners and M/s ECIL has been executed in  respect to 26 venues. Execution of contract for 
the remaining 10 venues, are in process. 
Recommendation 
2.9.7 T he Committee takes note of the fact that an Empowered Security Committee (ESC) has been 
constituted to co-ordinate, oversee and approv e the security arrangement for the Commonwealth 
Games 2010. 1n this regard, the Committee would like to recommend that coordination and 
monitoring need to be done at every level right upto the lowest level of security deployment. 
1ntelligence agencies should also be actively invo lved in coordination. There should not be any time 
gap in the dissemination and percolation of intelligence inputs. The Committee also recommends that 
the security personnel may be sensitized to be people-friendly.   
Action Taken 
2.9.8 The Commonwealth Games (CWG) are scheduled to be held from 3rd to 14th October, 2010. As 
per the “Host City Agreement”, all venues associated with the Commonwealth Games 20 I 0, are to be 
provided with specified facilities, including security. The security arrangements for the 
Commonwealth Games are being coordinated in the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) through two 
high level committee i.e. the Empowered Security Committee (ESC) under the Chairmanship of the 
Union Home Secretary and Commonwealth Game s Security Review Committee (CWGSRC) under 
the Chairpersonship of Special Secretary (CS). In this regard several meetings of ESC have been taken 
by Union Home Secretary, the latest being held on 25.11.2009, 17.12.2009, 16.02.2010, 03.03.2010, 
31.03.2010, 05.04.2010 and 06.04.2010. 
2.9.9 The Empowered Security Committee (ESC) has also constituted an International Security 
Liaison Group (ISLG) headed by Special Director IB with members of MEA; MoD; Cabinet 
Secretariat (R&AW); Delhi Police and Organizing Committee, Commonwealth Games, Delhi – 2010 
to share and address the security concerns of the participating countries and other stakeholders. 
2.9.10  Delhi police remains in regular touch with the Central Intelligence Agencies while making 
arrangements for the Commonwealth Games. Important intelligence inputs are promptly disseminated 
to all concerned for necessary action on the ground. Staff being deployed for the security and law and 
order arrangements during the Commonwealth Game s is being sensitized to be people-friendly and 
courteous and specific behavioral courses are being organized for them. 
Recommendation 
2.9.11  The Committee expresses its displeasure over the under-utilization of funds meant for 
modernization of Traffic and Communication Network for which Rs. 40 crore was allocated in BE 

2009-10 but only an amount of Rs. 10.63 crore could be utilized, which indicates serious lacunae in 
the implementation aspects of the project. It is a matter of great concern that the project was not 
initially timed to be completed before the Commonwealth Games 2010. The Committee is perturbed to 
note that the remaining amount has been appropriated for other purpose namely, ‘Delhi Police 
Building Programme’. (Para 3.11.8 ibid}  
Action Taken 
2.9.12  The project was approved by the Government only in August 2009. As such, as the project 
was at pre-investment stage with any physical implementation yet to take off during 2009-10, only an

2.9.13  The implementation of the project is being monitored regularly since the beginning by a 
Project Monitoring Group set up in the Ministry. Home Secretary had also taken several meetings 
with all stake-holders and sorted out various initial hurdles in the implementation of the project. 
2.10 REDRESSAL OF GRIEVANCES OF CISF DIRECT RECRUIT OFFICERS 
Recommendation 
2.10.1 The Committee, while noting the steps taken by the Government in regard to the redressal of 
‘grievances of Group ‘A’ CISF Officers, expresses its concern that despite the recommendations made 
in 54th, 5f1h, 83rd Reports of this Committee, the Nikhil Kumar Committee and Bhandari Committee 
recommendations and the few steps taken by MHA, the grievances of Group ‘A’ officers of CISF 
remain unresolved. There has been a severe attrition amongst these officers and the rest are totally 
demoralized. The very fact that many of them have been petitioning the authorities for the redressal of 
their grievances is a pointer for immediate action on the part of the Government (Para 3.14.3 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.10.2  The core issue raised by the offices in various fora including the Department Related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs is the problem of Direct Recruit Group ‘A’ 
Officers of CISF and this has arisen due to false impression on account of recruitment through Civil 
Services Examination conducted by the UPSC. 
2.10.3  On this issue Hon’ble Home Minister had assured the Lok Sabha on 20th December, 1999 that 
he would have a candid interaction with the CI SF officers and assured that if there were any 
grievances on the issue of parity, they would be removed. Accordingly, the Home Minister met the 
delegation in April, 2000 and July, 2000. 
2.10.4  Based on the discussions, MHA considered the issue through three different Committees, 
headed by senior level officers of the Ministry, na mely, (i) Shri V.S. Mathur, Spl. Secretary (ISP) in 
1997; (ii) Shri Nikhil Kumar, Spl. Secretary (ISP) in 1999; (iii) Shri S.K. Bhandari, Spl. Secretary 
(ISP) in 2001 were appointed to look into this issue. 
2.10.5  Based on the recommendation of the Committees the following action has been taken by the 
Government :- 
(a) The reduction in deputation quota of IPS offices in CPFs & consequent enhancement of 
promotion quota of departmental officers including Direct Recruit Group ‘A’ officers; 

(b) Reduction in the residency period for promotions to various ranks; 
(c) Grant of Senior Time Scale of (Rs.10,000-15,200) to Assistant Commandants (8,000-
13,500) after rendering 4 years of service; 
(d) Relaxation in 8 years - service requirement for deployment in UN Missions. 
2.10.6 As a result of the step taken by the Government the following Group ‘A’ Officers got 
promotion : 
(i) Senior Time Scale granted to 315 Group ‘A’ officers, including 93 Direct Recruits; 
(ii) 67 officers were promoted as Senior Commandants, including 12 Direct Recruits; 
(iii) 77 officers promoted as Commandants, including 15 Direct Recruits. 
(iv) 131 officers promoted as Dy. Commandants, including 75 Direct Recruits; 
(v) The Government also ordered the re-structuring for creation of higher level Group ‘A’ 
posts in order to further enhance their career prospects. Consequently, additional 80 
Group ‘A’ posts upto DIG level were sanctioned in December, 2004. Except 2 posts of 
DIG filled by deputation of IPS officers as per the Recruitment Rules, all the remaining 
posts have been filled by promotion of cadre officers of CISF. 
2.10.7  The aforesaid action taken by the Government was submitted in the form of note for the 
Cabinet and the Cabinet considered the same and approved the proposal in their meeting held on 
31.07.2006. 
2.10.8  Subsequently, MHA has also submitted Action Taken Report (ATR) to Rajya Sabha 
Secretariat in January, 2007. In the ATR, it ha s been clearly mentioned that career prospects of 
officers in CISF can be compared only with simila rly placed officers in ot her Central Police Forces, 
and the former i.e. CISF are not in disadvantageous position in the matter of career progression. Their 
career has nowhere been blocked, but on the other hand, all of them have already got promotions in 
higher ranks. 
Recommendation 
2.10.9  The Committee urges upon the Government to implement the scheme at the earliest so that the

the 4 training institutions of BSF, ITBP and NSG. Th is figure reflects the number of personnel whose 
training are organized through BPR&D. However,  these figures do not include the number of 
personnel trained in ‘Commando Course’ by thes e CPMFs in respect of their own personnel. 
Likewise, number of State Police Personnel trained in ‘Commando Course, in their own State. Police 
Training Institutes has also not been reflected in  this chart (Annexure-IV). Accordingly, the actual 
number of personnel trained in ‘Commando Course’ is higher. 
Recommendation 
2.12.8  The Committee believes that in addition to the information furnished by the Ministry of Home 
Affairs to it, there would be more specialized training centres in some States, particularly the Naxal 
affected States, to impart commando training to the forces, but their numbers would be miniscule as 
compared to the need of training of 8.5 % of th e total strength of the State Police Forces. While 
surfing the net, the Committee came across the information relating to a training centres for jungle 
warfare located in Kanker (Chhattisgarh) and an other training centre Chandaka (Orissa) and yet 
another recently set up by Government of Maharashtra to train the recently raised Force One battalion 
of Maharashtra Police.                                                                                   (Para 3.17.10 ibid) 
Action Taken 

2.12.9  The Government has approved setting up of 20 Counter Insurgency & Anti-Terrorist (CIAT) 
Schools in naxal affected States. Funds for 15 such CIAT Schools has been released by the Central 
Government so far. 
Recommendation 
2.12.10  The Committee also learnt that the Central Government proposed to set up an Advanced 
Training Centre for CRPF Commandos in Uttar Pradesh. The Government of Bihar is also reported 
to have plan to set up four institutes to impart training in counter insurgency and jungle warfare.(Para 3.17.11 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.12.11  There is no proposal from CRPF for setting up of Advanced Training Centre in Uttar 
Pradesh. As regards, Bihar, the Government of India has already approved setting up of four 
temporary Counter-Insurgency and An ti-Terrorist Schools in Bihar un der the Plan Schemes to train 
their personnel. 
Recommendation 
2.12.12  Be that as it may, the Committee, therefore, with all the emphasis at its command, urges upon 
the Ministry of Home Affairs to take this aspect of commando training seriously and reformulate its 
Policy on Education and Training of Central Police Forces with a view to ensuring that adequate 
number of police personnel, especially trained in commando, counter insurgency, anti-terrorist and 
guerrilla warfare, are available to counter the menace of terrorism, insurgency and left wing 
extremism in all their hues. Besides, the inadequacies in training infrastructure, the Committee has 
been given to understand that there is shortage of trainers and the Government should look into this 
aspect by recruiting sufficient number of trainers and also updation of the Training of trainers’ 
programme. The Central Government may also proactively assists the State Government particularly 
those affected by cross-border terrorism, insurgency and left wing extremism, in setting up Training 
Centres for training their police personnel in guerilla and jungle warfare and help them set up special 
units like the Greyhound of Andhra Pradesh Police and COBRA of CRPF.  
(Para 3.17.12 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.12.13  Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) is already taking steps to train State 
Police personnel in Commando, Coun ter-Insurgency, Anti-Terrorist and Guerrila Warfare etc. at the 
Central Police Training Institutions and with the help of Integrated HQ of Ministry of Defence 
(Army). 
2.12.14  Every year BPR&D allots more than 3000 slots to the States in the training courses on 
Counter Insurgency & Commando, Bomb Disposal, Weapons & Tactics, Anti-Terrorist & VIP 
Protection Commando, Counter Insurgency & Jungle Warfare and Counter Left Wing Extremist etc. 
as per details at Annexure-IV, in training scheduled/regular courses at the Central Police Training 
Institutions and Indian Army. 
2.12.15  The Indian Army has also been providing training in Counter Naxal and Explosives etc. to 
the State Police personnel. They have trained 38646 State Police Personnel during the last five years. 
(Annexure-V). 

2.12.16  The Indian Army has also given more than 5500 training slots in Counter Naxal and 
Explosives for training of State Police Personnel during the year 2010-11. (Annexure-VI). 
2.12.17  The Government of India has already approved setting up of a Central Academy for Police 
Training at Bhopal. Besides, training directly recr uited Dy. Superintendents of Police of the State 
Police Forces, this Academy will also conduct cour ses on ‘Training of Trainers, programme’ for the 
benefit of State Police Personnel. 
2.12.18  The Finance Co mmission has approved Rs.2160 crore (A nnexure-VII) for strengthening of 
existing Police Institutes and construction of new Training Centres in the States. This will enhance 
capabilities of the State for providing training to their Police Personnel. 
2.13 NAXALISM 
Recommendation 
2.13.1  It is public knowledge that the Maoists have become an impediment to development projects in 
most backward regions and tribal dominated forest areas and are running parallel administrations, 
siphoning money from government funds and indulging in extortion from local people, contractors 
and others. The Maoists propagate that administrative and political institutions are inadequate; 
espouse local demands; take advantage .of the prevalent dissatisfaction and feeling of injustice among 
exploited segments of the population and claim to form an alternative utopian Government. The 
Committee understands that by providing livelihood, land and proper wages, with good governance 
and proper utilization of funds allocated to the respective States for various government sponsored 
development schemes, people could be weaned away from naxalism and this menace could be 
contained. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that the approach to the naxalite problem needs a 
blend of firm handling with sensitive approach to the developmental aspects. The Government should 
also involve the political parties, people’s representatives, Panchayati Raj institutions and above all 
the masses, in all its initiatives to contain the menace. (Para 4.10.1 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.13.2  The Government has adopted an integrated approach in dealing with LWE activities in the 
arenas of security, development and public perception. State Governments deal with the various issues 
related to naxalites activities in the States. The Central Government supplements their efforts over a 
wide range of schemes. 
Recommendation 
2.13.3 The Committee is of the view that capacity building is required to be done in the agriculture 
sector, bringing in modern technologies, so that th e young people in the ar eas affected by LWE are 
able to take up agriculture for a gainful employment. (Para 4.10.2 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.13.4  Modern Technologies in the form of hybrid and improved seeds, farm mechanization, 
cultivation practices like SRI, pest management and nutrient management techniques, protected 
cultivation etc. have been developed by various institutions under Ministry of Agriculture and under 
development programmes of the Ministry. These modern technologies are required to be taken up in 
Left Wing Extremist affected areas also. This is being done but can be further enhanced by State 
Governments under various programmes of the Ministry. Funds are also provided to State 

Governments and implementing agencies for capacity building, training in latest technologies and 
demonstration, so that young people are able to take up agriculture for gainful employment in the 
country including in the areas affected by Left Wing Extremism. 
Recommendation 
2.13.5  The Committee understands that most of the habitations in the affected areas are devoid of 
electricity, which makes them an easy haven for the extremists. Therefore, the Government should 
start a new programme of electrifying all the habitations in the extremist-affected areas with specific 
targets fixed. Electricity is a basic requirement in the modern days and once this is available, people 
will be able to take up various activities for gainful employment and children will be able to devote 
their time for studies, etc. 
(Para 4.10.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.13.6 All the projects in the Left Wing Extremism districts have been sanctioned under RGGVY. The 
projects are under different stages of implementation. MNRE is mandated to electrify habitations 
having population less than 100. Therefore, there is no need to launch any new scheme. 
Recommendation 
2.13.7  It is a fact that in naxal violence, people, from all sides, including the local people, extremists 
as well as the security forces lose their lives. Though the multi-pronged development strategy is 
required to be planned and implemented, it should also be kept in one’s mind that violence also needs 
to be addressed. Everyone knows that people in the affected areas do not support the movement by 
their heart but circumstances, coercion and the under-development make them surrender to the 
movement. Therefore, while taking up developmental activities, the strategies, as per the area and 
location, will have to be adopted to counter the violent activities. One particular strategy will not help 
for all the areas and States. There needs to be a coordination between the Central para-military 
forces and the State security organizations. While preparing strategy for such operations by security 
forces, sufficient training should be given before sending them to the field for facing the extremists. In 
fact, the local-youth are the right persons, who know the topography of the areas. Therefore, local 
youth on a large scale should be involved through employment in the police forces and CPMFs for 
operations within those areas to resist any attack from the extremists. Police force should be 
modernized in terms of latest and modern weaponry, communication, mobility and infrastructure. 
They should be supplied more Mine Protected Vehicles and the Central Para Military Forces should 
be deployed on long-term basis.   
Action Taken 
2.13.8  Government has adopted an integrated appr oach in dealing with LWE activities in the arenas 
of security, development and public perception. State Governments deal with the various issues 
related to naxalites activities in the States. The Central Government supplements their efforts over a 
wide range of schemes. 
2.13.9  The Government has decided to set up Counter Insurgency and Anti-Terrorism Schools 
(CIATS), to begin with in the States of Assam, Jharkhand, Bihar, Orissa and Chhattisgarh under a 
centrally sponsored scheme in the 11th Plan period for providing training to the State police personnel 

of these States in Counter-Insurgency and Anti-Terrorism  with a view to tackle the menace of 
naxalism insurgency. Approval has been granted to establish 20 CIAT Schools, 04 each in five States 
of Assam, Jharkhand, Bihar, Orissa and Chhattisgarh. The Ministry of Home Affairs would provide an 
amount of Rs. l.5 crore to each school for develo pment of temporary infrastructure. The Ministry 
would also bear recurring expenditure towards honorarium to be paid to the trainers. 
2.13.10  The Government has sanctioned 13,566 Special Police Officers (SPOs) to the Left Wing 
Extremism affected States. The State Government  appoints these SPOs by locally recruiting them. 
These SPOs act as a guide to the police force as they are local and have better knowledge of the 
terrain. They are a source of loca l intelligence and some State Governments have given them training 
in use of arms. 
2.13.11  To supplement the efforts of the State Governments in modernizing their police forces, the 
Ministry of Home Affairs has been implementing Scheme for Modernization of State Police Forces 
towards capacity building of the State Police Forces , especially for meeting the emerging challenges 
to internal security in the form of terrorism, naxalism, etc. 
Recommendation 
2.13.12  The Committee also feels that the Central Para Military Forces trained in guerilla warfare 
should be deployed in all the sensitive districts of the affected areas. There should be more Counter 
Insurgency and Jungle Warfare (CIJW) Colleges opened on the lines of Vairengte in Mizoram and 
another training centre at Kanker in Chhattisgarh, for training of Police Personnel for counter-
insurgency operations. The Committee understands that the biggest limitation while conducting 
counter-naxal operations, is the lack of helicopt er support from the Go vernment. The Government 
should therefore provide helicopter support for conducting operations and for reconnaissance.(Para 4.10.12 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.13.13  At present, besides 06 CRPF SAF (COBRA) Units, 67 CPMF Battalions have been deployed 
in the sensitive districts/areas of 09 LWE affected States (i.e. Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, 
Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Mahara shtra, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal). These Battalions 
are carrying out joint operations in conjunction with State Police to support the State authorities in 
countering the naxal menace. For training purpos es, the Central Government has already sanctioned 
04 Counter Insurgency Anti-Terrorists (CIAT) Schools each for 04 naxal affected States i.e. Bihar, 
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Orissa. The amount for 03 CIAT schools to be established in each of 
these States has been already sanctioned and released  to the States. Further, a total of 07 helicopters 
i.e. 04 MI-17 helicopters of Indian Air Force and 03 DHRUV helicopters of BSF have been already 
positioned in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh to prov ide necessary air support to the ground forces 
deployed in these focused States. 
Recommendation 
2.13.14  Money is the life-line of every extremist activit y. Therefore, all the channels from which the 
naxalites get funding, should be blocked. There should be a proper mechanism to investigate and 
check the extortion rackets being run by the naxalites and to punish all those who are found guilty of 
funding naxalites. 
(Para 4.10.15 ibid) 

Action Taken 
2.13.15  ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ being State su bjects, action with respect to maintenance of law 
and order lies primarily in the do main of the concerned State Governments, who deal with the various 
issues related to naxalites activities in the States. The Central Government also closely monitors the 
situation and supplements their efforts in several ways, both on security and development fronts. 
2.14 UNION TERRITORIES WITH LEGISLATURE  
Recommendation 
2.14.1  The Committee takes serious note that Plan allocation for the year 2010-11 has been reduced 
by 30% from RE 2009-10. This is bound to affect several schemes. The Committee desires that the 
Ministry of Home Affairs may take up the issue with the Planning Commission for enhancement of the 
Plan allocation at the RE stage so that no projects suffer for want of finance. (Para 5.2.3 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.14.2  The decline in the overall Plan allocation is mainly due to reduced allocation under Tsunami 
Rehabilitation Programme. The allocation under TRP was Rs.755.02 crore within the overall Plan 
allocation of Rs.1536.81 crore in BE 2009-10 wher eas the allocation under TRP is Rs.100 crore only 
within the overall Plan allocation of Rs.954.36 crore in BE 2010-11. 
2.14.3  Planning Commission has subsequently agreed and recommended to Ministry of Finance to 
enhance the Plan allocation by Rs.332.97 crore to Rs.1291.35 crore. Ministry of Home Affairs had 
also requested the Ministry of Finance in this regard and the Ministry of Finance has assured that it 
will be considered in RE stage, keeping in view the pace of expenditure and the overall availability of 
savings at that stage for re-allocation to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. 
Recommendation 
2.14.4  The Committee notes that the budgetary provision for Tsunami Rehabilitation Programme has 
been reduced to Rs. 100 crore in BE 2010-11 in comparison to Rs. 647.77 crore in RE 2009-10. The 
Committee presumes that major part of the rehabilitation programme must have been completed in 
Andaman & Nicobar Islands. In case the allocation is not sufficient for the purpose, efforts be made 
for enhancing the provision at the RE stage. The Committee feels that due to reduction in allocation 
for Tsunami Rehabilitation, the remaining part of the rehabilitation programme should not suffer.(Para 5.2.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.14.5  Out of the approved package of Rs.2654.69 under TRP, the UT Administration of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands has utilized Rs.2429.14 crore till March 2010. The Empowered Group of Ministers on 
TRP had, in its meeting held on 11.02.2010, decided that in case of Andaman & Nicobar Islands, 
Planning Commission will assess requirement of funds to be met through Plan provision and no 
further funds would be provided under TRP. 
2.14.6  Subsequently, Planning Commission has agreed and recommended to Ministry of Finance to 
enhance the allocation to Rs.203.31 crore for ongoing tsunami related projects. Ministry of Finance 
has assured that it will be considered at RE stage, keeping in view the pace of expenditure and the 
overall availability of savings at that stage for re-allocation to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. 

2.15 GENERAL RECOMMENDATION 
Recommendation 
2.15.1  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:–– 
As per the criteria fixed for quantity, calorie and protein under Mid-day Meal Scheme, the ceiling of 
Rs.6.60 is not sufficient for the children of the A&N Islands as the prices of essential commodities in 
the Islands is the highest in the country due to its remoteness. The ceiling needs to be increased to 
Rs.10-15 in view of the prevailing market rates. [Para 5.5. 1 (vii) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.2  UT Administration has increased the ceiling of Mid-day Meal for Primary and Middle from 
Rs. 5.88 to Rs.6.02 (for Primary) and from Rs.6. 02 to Rs.7.02 (for middle) from the current session 
i.e. 2010-11. UT Administration has no proposal to enhance the ceiling further. 
2.15.3  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:- 
Mid-day Meal Scheme may be extended from class VIII to XII in consonance with the facility extended 
in Lakshdweep, Delhi and Tamil Nadu; [Para 5.5.1 (viii) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.4  Cooked Mid Day meal programme is a centrally aided programme and as per this programme, 
the scheme is applicable to studen ts of Class I to VIII only. UT Ad ministration is not in favour of 
extending it up to class XII. 
Recommendation 
2.15.5  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:- 
Hostels in Islands particularly in remote backwar d areas like Mayabunder Boy’s Hostel are in a 
dilapidated condition. The entire Islands fall under Seismic Zone V and these hostels may crumble in 
case of any earthquake, causing loss of lives. Therefore, hostels in Rangat, Diglipur, Kishorinagar are 
in dire need of repair/renovation. There are many schools having broken tin roofs, broken thatched 
walls with no pucca floor, drinking water and toilet facilities. Those schools should properly be 
constructed with all basic amenities. Some schools in the islands do not have class rooms, science 
labs, and staff quarters. These facilities must be provided immediately; [Para 5.5.1 (ix) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.6  There is a token provision in Annual Plan 2010-11 for renovation of hostels at Mayabunder, 
Swarajgram in Diglipur, Kishorinagar etc. APWD ha s been requested to initiate the works on priority 
basis. 
2.15.7  In Annual Plan 2010-11, token provision exists for repair of 381 classrooms as against 1466 
classrooms which need major/minor repairs. Repair  works of other classrooms will be initiated in 
subsequent plans in phased manner. 

2.15.8  Additional fund requirement for both school buildings and hostels has been projected by the 
UT Administration to the Planning Commission. 
Recommendation 
2.15.9  The Committee is of the view that be sides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions: 
Since 2008 bicycles are be ing provided to Nicobari  ST students in Class VIII under Sarva Shikhsha 
Abhiyan. Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Puducherry are providing free bicycles to all the 
students. A& N Islands is considered as mini India on account of having harmony among different 
castes and creeds. Students have to walk 10-12 kms to come to main road for buses and students are 
not getting timely reimbursement for their bus passes. Therefore, bicycles should be provided to all 
the students to avoid any discrimination between tribals and non-tribals. [Para 5.5.1 (x) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.10  Under Sarva Shikhsha Abhiyan (SSA), bicycles are provided to Boys and Girls of class VIII 
belonging to Scheduled Tribes, whose schools are at a distance of 1.5 km and more from their 
residences. The objective is to encourage tribal children to attend schools. However, UT 
Administration will explore the possibility to provide bicycles to all students who qualify their 10th 
class examination with B1 & above grades of mark s i.e. 70% or above in order to encourage better 
performance amongst students. 
Recommendation 
2.15.11  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions: 
Old age pension of Rs.500/- was last revised in 2005-06. Goa and Delhi have revised the pension to 
Rs.1000/-   in the year 2008. Besides dhoti, Saree and four kg. rice per month is also given by Tamil 
Nadu Government. Old persons in A&N Islands should be given pension of Rs.l 000/- per month. They 
should also be given two dhotis/Sarees in a year. [Para 5.5.1 (xi) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.12  The recommendations of the Committee for enhancement of pension under various schemes 
are being examined by the UT Administration, keeping in view funds position. The additional funds 
required are Rs.8.40 crore per annum. 
2.15.13  UT Administration is not in favour of providing two dhotis/sarees in a year. 
Further Recommendation 
2.15.14  The Committee desires that an early decision may be taken in regard to enhancement of 
pension under various schemes. 
Recommendation 
2.15.15  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:–– 
Destitute/single/abandoned/divorced women in Delhi are getting a pension of Rs.1000/- per month. 
No such scheme has been extended to A&N Islands. Pension of Rs.1000/- for 

destitute/single/abandoned/divorced women in A&N Islands should be given. Government of NCT 
Delhi provides marriage assistance of Rs.20000/- to orphan girls and daughters of widows. This 
scheme should also be extended to A&N Islands. 
[Para 5.5.1 (xiii) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.16  A new scheme for providing an allowance of Rs. 1000/- per month to unemployed, single and 
destitute women has been formulated and is under consideration for implementation by the UT 
Administration during Annual Plan 2010-11. UT Administration is not in favour of providing 
marriage assistance of Rs.20,000/- to orphan girls and daughters of widows. 
Recommendation 
2.15.17  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:- 
There are 1400 Anganwadi Workers and Helpers.  Workers are getting Rs.1800-2000 while the 
helpers are getting Rs.990/- per month. These Workers/Helpers are working since the last 15 to 20 
years. Puducherry and Tamil Nadu Governments have granted regular pay scales to them. Tamil 
Nadu Government also pay HRA, City Allowan ce and medical reimbursement. Workers/Helpers 
should be given at least minimum wages till such time, regular pay-scale for them are granted.[Para 5.5.1 (xiv) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.18  Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary, part-time workers and not regular 
Government employees. 
2.15.19  UT Administration is not in favour of enhancing Honorarium to Anganwadi workers and 
helpers or to provide regular pay scales. 
Further Recommendation 
2.15.20  The Anganwadi workers and Anganwadi helpers  are the backbone of Integrated Child 
Development Services Scheme. An increase in the remuneration of Anganwadi workers from 
Rs. 1,500 per month to Rs. 3,000 per month and for Anganwadi helpers from Rs. 750 per month 
to Rs. 1,500 per month was announced by the Un ion Finance Minister in his Budget (2011-12) 
speech with the likelihood of  improving lives of around 22 lakh Anganwadi workers and 
helpers. The Committee is of the view that th e UT Administration also should enhance 
Honorarium of Anganwadi workers and helpers, as has been promised in the Union Budget 
(2011-12). 
Recommendation 
2.15.21  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the. 
Government should also consider the following suggestions: 
Yatri Niwas/Dharamshala run by  Municipal Corporation was c onstructed 50 years ago. However, 
with the increase in population, no additional rooms have been added in spite of foundation stone laid 
down by the then Union Minister of State for Home Affairs. Municipal Corporation should be 
provided funds for construction of Dharamshala.                                               [Para 5.5. 1 (xviii) ibid] 
Action Taken 

2.15.22  The foundation stone for construction of a Yatri Niwas at Phoenix Bay was laid by the then 
Union Minister of State for Home Affairs on 06.04.2000. A proposal for CRZ clearance was sent. 
However, after the tsunami of 2004 , the site is affected by tidal action and hence it was not 
considered appropriate by the UT Administration to go ahead and pursue the CRZ clearance for this 
site. Consequently, the Revenue Department was requested to allot an alternate land at Anarkali. 
Allotment of suitable land for construction of Yatri Niwas is being pursued. 
2.15.23  At present the Yatri Niwas at Haddo has 1 dormitory and 6 rooms. The Yatri Niwas at 
Delanipur has 8 rooms with common toilet at affordable rates. 
Recommendation 
2.15.24  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions: 
Police Personnel in the A&N Islands should be granted Ration Money like their counterparts in Delhi 
Police and CRPF.    [Para 5.5.1 (xxi) ibid] 
Action Taken 
2.15.25  The proposal was examined but was not agreed to by the Integrated Finance Division of this 
Ministry. However, the same is being taken up with IFD (H). 
Further Recommendation 
2.15.26  The Committee desires to be apprised of the reasons for not agreeing to the proposal by 
Integrated Finance Division (IFD) of the Minist ry. The Committee may be informed of the final 
decision of IFD and the present status thereof. 
Recommendation 
2.15.27  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions:- 
About 80,000 agitated educated youth are jobless. Group ‘D’ Posts in various departments of A&N 
Islands Administration has been banned. The youth in the Islands does not have job opportunities as 
compared to their counterparts in the mainland. Therefore, special attention needs to be paid for 
employment of youth in the Islands.   
Action Taken 
2.15.28  UT Administration has informed that with the implementation of CCS (RP) Rules, 2008, all 
Group ‘D’ posts have been upgraded to Group ‘C’. 
2.15.29  As per Live Register of Employment Exchange, Port Blair there are around 40,000 male and 
female registrants. Further scope for employment in Government Sector is limited; relative to the size 
of the economy, it is already quite substantial. Th erefore the UT Administration has put considerable 
focus on developing and implementing skill oriented training programmes. As a part of flagship 
programme of Skill Development Mission of GOI, the UT Administration’s mission is to train jobless 
youth to enable them to get employed/ take up self-employment during the mission period (2008-
2012). Under this scheme, 25 Vocational Training Providers have registered so far and 1700 youth 
were already trained and given NCVT certificate af ter being tested in different trades such as 

agriculture, fisheries, tourism and short-term engineering trades. ITI, Dollygunj is the sole 
Government Institute providing vocational training in 10 engineering trades. Special efforts are taken 
to place trainees through placement process. 
2.15.30  Vocational Guidance and Career Programme in different parts of A & N Islands for the 
unemployed youth. The Employment and Training Department also conduct camps with financial 
Agencies/Departments who are extending loans to unemployed youth for self-employment. 
2.15.31  Fisheries are one of the prime sectors offering ample scope for employment in the islands. 
The Fisheries Department is already implementing various schemes/ programmes, whereby financial 
assistance and training is extended to the local youths to take up various fisheries related activities as 
self-employment. Schemes presently implemented are as under :- 
1. Subsidy for construction of mechanised/motorised boats. 
2. Subsidy for purchase of fish transport vehicles/deep freezers. 
3. Deputing local youths to mainland for training in Fisheries-related activities. 
4. Subsidy for purchase/construction of deep sea fishing vessels and purchase of deep 
freezers under RKVY. 
5. New programmes are also in the pipeline under RKVY to encourage setting up of ice 
plants, cold storages and fish retail outlets in the islands by the interested unemployed 
youths. 
2.15.32  The Industries Department of UT Administration also provides financial assistance through 
Prime Minister Employment Guarantee Scheme (PMEGP) to educate unemployed youth. 
2.15.33  Co-operative societies promoted and managed by unemployed youth are being encouraged 
with a view to generate employment avenues, especially in the field of construction, tourism, contract 
etc. At present 281 Co-operative Societies with more than 3000 youths as member, having paid-up 
share capital of Rs.38.21 lakhs have been formed by the educated/ unemployed youth of this UT, of 
which 82 societies have been organised and registered during 2008-2009 and 2009-2010. The UT 
Administration provides financial assistance to the needy and eligible Co-operative societies in the 
shape of working capital loan, share capital loan, loan-cum subsidy, managerial subsidy, grant-in-aid 
for infrastructure development etc. as per approved pattern of assistance. 
Recommendation 
2.15.34  The Committee is of the view that besides the specific recommendations made above, the 
Government should also consider the following suggestions: 
According to BPL Census 2000, BPL famiiies in Nicobar Tribal Area were 67%, South Andaman 
District 13%, North Andaman District 7%. Many families living in de-reserved blocks or jungles in 
North and Middle Andamans have been left out in BPL list. The cut off score for identifying BPL 
families is discriminatory. As per Planning Commission there should be 28000 BPL cards whereas 
only 17000 BPL/AY cards have been issued. Remaining 11000 BPL cards should be issued 
immediately.  
[Para 5.5.1 (xxv) ibid] 

Action Taken 
2.15.35  BPL Census is carried out by the UT Administration as per the guidelines issued by the 
Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD). The numbers of rural poor so derived are restricted to 
poverty estimates of the Planning Commission and States/UTs are given the flexibility of increase 
upto 10% more than the Planning Commission’s estimate. 
2.15.36 The Planning Commission poverty estimate 1999-2000 for A & N Islands was 11600 BPL 
families; MoRD had communicated 14600 BPL families for BPL Census 2002. BPL families in A & 
N Islands are 15768. 
2.15.37 Initially, the BPL census covered only re venue villages, but there are some encroached 
pockets of forest lands. These areas were also e numerated in the survey but were not taken into 
account while finalising the BPL list. 
2.15.38  The cut-off score of 18 was fixed for Andaman District and 33 for Nicobar District taking 
into consideration that Nicobar District is at a di sadvantage compared to Andaman District due to the 
remoteness and with a predominant tribal population.

BPL population to total population and % of BPL population to total population in rural areas for the 
years 1997 and 2002 are given below:

2.20 CENSUS 2011 AND NATIONAL POPULATION REGISTER 
Recommendation 
2.20.1  The Committee observes that the first phase of the Census 2011 will be held during April and 
September 2010 for collection of data on Houselisting and Housing Census as well as for preparation 
of National Population Register. The Committee apprehends that it will be difficult and improper to 
carry out both exercises together for the following reasons: 
(i) The Census information is collected under the Census Act, 1948 which guarantees 
complete confidentiality of the individual and household data collected. This 
confidentiality clause is known to be a key-stone that ensures accuracy and sanctity of 
the Census Data; and 
(ii) The National Population Register (NPR) information is to be collected under the 
Citizenship Act, 1955 read with the Citizenship (Registration and Issue of National 
Identity Cards) Rules, 2003 and the data collected are not confidential and are meant to 
be used for identifying individuals and household. These make the purpose, objectives 
and the process of the two exercise different and, hence, it is important to keep the two 
exercises separate in order to maintain sanctity of both. (Para 6.9.2 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.20.2  The Committee has rightly observed that the Census information is collected under the Census 
Act, 1948 and the National Population Register (NPR) information is to be collected under the 
Citizenship Act, 1955 read with the Citizenship (Registration and Issue of National Identity Cards) 
Rules, 2003. Keeping the distinct nature of both these activities, separate Notifications have been 
made under both the Acts. Similarly, two distinct questionnaires have been designed for NPR and 
Housing Census. The two questionnaires have only 2 questions in common - Name of the Head of the 
Household and Sex of the Head of the Household. The enumerators appointed to carry out the 
enumeration have also been appointed under appropriate sections of both the Acts namely, Section 
4(2) of the Census Act 1948 and Rule 5 of the Citi zenship (Registration and Issue of National Identity 
Cards) Rules, 2003. Instructions manual for the two are separate and separate honorarium is being 
given for the two exercises. Only the infrastructure of the Census is being used for NPR. In all other 
respects, the NPR is a distinct exercise. In othe r words, the NPR exercise is piggybacking on the 
Census exercise. 

2.20.3  The Committee has rightly pointed out that the information gathered for Housing Census under 
the Census Act, 1948 is kept confidential. The Housing Census questionnaire carries a legend 
“Confidential when Filled”. The NPR Questionnaire do es not carry this legend. In fact, data collected 
under NPR will be published in the local areas during the process of authentication. 
2.20.4  Thus all efforts have been made to keep the two exercises separate and maintain the sanctity of 
both. 
2.21 HOUSING SCHEMES FOR DELHI POLICE 
Recommendation 
2.21.1  The Committee feels that on the one hand Delhi Police faces scarcity of housing for its 
personnel and on the other the funds allocated, particularly non-plan allocation, are not spent fully. 
During 2006-07 only a fraction was spent whereas in 2007-08 and 2008-09, more than 10 per cent 
could not be spent. For achieving physical targets, achieving financial targets is necessary. Delhi 
Police should take necessary steps to achieve financial targets.  (Para 7.7.3 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.21.2  The physical targets set under housing for Delhi Police were difficult to be met in the earlier 
years due to time taken in getting land from land owning agencies and in getting subsequent 
clearances from them as well as from other civic agen cies. Consequently, there had been difficulty in 
meeting the financial targets as well. 
2.21.3  Delhi Police has now set the physical targets more realistically. Out of 15 projects targeted to 
be completed till 31.03.2010, 12 projects for construction of 469 staff quarters and 15 office buildings 
(5 PS, 3 PP, 1 EOW building and 6 buildings of office block/barracks/MT Block) had been completed. 
The expenditure on this account was Rs.94.00 crore out of an allocation of Rs.121.00 crore under both 
Plan and Non-Plan. Remaining 3 projects for construction of 104 staff quarters, 3 PS and 1 Office 
building have been completed by 30.06.2010. 
2.21.4  Target for completion of 23 staff quarters has been set in Action Plan 2010-11 of the Ministry 
in addition to targets for completion for clearance formalities and floating of tender for other projects. 
The physical and financial progress of these projects, are closely monitored through a Project 
Monitoring Committee set up in the Ministry under Ad ditional Secretary (UT). 7 meetings have been 
held so far on 23.10.2009, 06.11.2009, 24.11.2009, 23.12.2009, 26.02.2010, 07.05.2010 and 
23.06.2010. Delhi Police had also taken up similar action by holding monitoring meetings with all 
land-owning/civic agencies and executing agencies. 
Recommendation 
2.21.5  The Committee feels that for achieving 40 per cent satisfaction level, present allocations both 
Plan and Non~Plan - are not sufficient. Government should therefore assess the total requirement of 
funds. Allocations should be increased to enable  Delhi Police to achieve desired satisfaction within 
the next five years.    (Para 7.7.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 

2.21.6  The observation of the Committee has been noted. The actual requirement of funds of Delhi 
Police is assessed each year at the finalization of th e RE of the current year  and the next year BE. 
DP’s projections based on the stages of each project and new projects to be taken up are examined and 
proposed to the Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission. 
Recommendation 
2.21.7  The Committee does not understand why Delhi Police makes such a target which cannot be 
achieved. During tenth plan 40% satisfaction le vel was proposed and only 22.91% was achieved. 
Again 40% is being proposed for Eleventh Plan. This is not a right approach. Delhi Police should try 
to keep realistic targets only.    
Action Taken 
2.21.8  Target was to achieve higher satisfaction level in Tenth Five Year Plan period as well as 
Eleventh Five Year Plan period but due to a sign ificant increase in sanctioned strength of Delhi Police 
personnel from 64,645 in March 2007 to 83,740 the satisfaction level of housing could not increase as 
targeted. In addition, there are other factors also as mentioned below due to which the targeted 
housing satisfaction level has not been achieved :–– 
(i) Delay in allotment of land by land owning agencies.  
(ii) Delay in clearance of building plans by  local bodies like DDA, MCD, NDMC, Delhi 
Fire Service & DUAC etc. in time. 
(iii) Non completion of constructions by the executing agencies in time in certain cases. 
(iv) Non allotment of ready built flats by DDA. 
2.21.9  Delhi Police, however, has been advised to set the physical targets realistically raking into 
account the above factors. 
Recommendation 
2.21.10  The Committee desires that the pitfalls of the Tenth Plan have to be avoided and the physical 
targets fixed for the Eleventh Five-Year Plan should be achieved. Clearance of proposals and 
clearance for lands may be taken up at the highest level so that these areas do not act as impediments 
for the achievement of targets.   
Action Taken 
2.21.11  The matter was continuously pursued with land owning agencies for allotment of land for 
construction of Residential Buildings and purchase of ready built flats. So as to achieve the physical 
targets fixed for Eleventh Five Year Plan period, the MHA has constituted a Project Monitoring 
Committee (PMC) under the Chairpersonship of AS(UT). The PMC has fixed targets with regard to 
obtaining mandatory clearances from civic bodies, finalization of tender documents by the Executing 
Agencies and completion of the projects under Plan Head as well as Non Plan Head (PMS) during 
Current Financial Year 2010-11 in consultation with all the concerned agencies in its monthly 
meeting. Wherever necessary, the issues requiring attentio n are also taken up at the level of HS/HM. 
Delhi Police is also holding fortnightly meetings with Executing Agencies and civic bodies to 
review/monitor the progress of Delhi Police projects included in Action Plan 2010-11. 
Recommendation 

2.21.12   All the projects, which are under way in both Plan and Non-Plan Schemes, may be 
completed as per the targets and there should not be any cost and time over-runs. (Para 7.7.10 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.21.13   An Annual Action Plan-2010-11 covering projects of Plan Head and Non Plan Head (PMS) 
has been drawn in consultation with the executi ng agencies and the civic bodies wherein a time 
schedule has been fixed with regard to obtaining mandatory clearances from civic bodies, finalization 
of tender documents by executing Agencies and completion of projects during 2010-11. The progress 
of each project is closely monitored through the Project Monitoring Committee set up in MHA under 
the Chairpersonship of AS(UT). It has been impressed upon all concerned to achieve the given targets 
to avoid cost and time over runs. 
Recommendation 
2.21.14  The Committee was given to understand that one of the reasons for the shortfall in the 
housing project was non-completion of construction by PWD in time. The Committee takes strong 
exception to this. If PWD does not improve its perf ormance, Delhi Police may go in for construction 
by other public sector undertakings.   
Action Taken 
2.21.15  Delhi Police after seeking prior approval of MHA, has handed over the construction work of 
27 Projects to PSUs (22 Projects to M/s RITES and 05 Projects to M/s HPL). The time frame has been 
fixed for completion of each project. In case of delay at any stage, a suitable penalty clause has also 
been included in the agreement so signed with the concerned PSUs. The progress of existing projects 
being executed by PWD are closely monitored through the PMC set up in MHA under AS(UT). The 
PMC meetings are attended by repr esentatives of PWD. In addition to regular meetings of PMC, a 
separate meeting was held with Secretary, PWD, GNCTD on 06.11.2009 to discuss exclusively the 
projects being implemented by PWD.

Officers of the CPMFs so that proj ects do not get stuck of the implementation stage. The problems 
faced by CPMFs for clearance from lo cal bodies are also discussed and in case of any difficulties, the 
issues are addressed at the appropriate level with the agencies/officials concerned in States. There are 
certain construction / land acquisition related issues  which are also incorporated in the Action Plan 
formulated by Ministry of Home Affairs and are re viewed periodically by the Divisional Heads and 
also at highest level. The items/issues which are in Action Plan are taken up with the concerned 
agencies/ officials regularly so as to meet the deadlines/ timelines fixed for such items. Hence, the 
requisite mechanism is already available in the Mini stry to ensure the disposal of proposals on fast 
track basis. 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER-III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
3.1 MODERNISATION OF STATE POLICE FORCE (MPF) 
3.1.1 The Committee is unhappy to note that there is no Management Information System (MIS) for 
proper monitoring and concurrent evaluation of the Scheme of Modernisation of Police Forces. Now 
that the CMC has offered to develop the software on the lines of MISs done for the other centrally 
sponsored programmes of the Government of India, the Ministry should take immediate steps to firm 
up the project so that a scientific monitoring mechanism of the scheme is in place at the earliest. 
(Para 3.1.11 of 144th Report) 
Action Taken 
3.1.2 The CMC Ltd. was selected for the job to develop a Management Information System (MIS) 
for monitoring implementation of MPF Scheme. It has submitted a technical proposal to Ministry of 
Home Affairs in which it has projected a high cost for developing the software. Further, it has sought 
12 months time from the date of entrustment of the job to complete the project. Hence, the Ministry is 
exploring an alternative to develop a less costly similar to the requirement of the PM Division and 
user friendly MIS software like the one developed by Department of Land Resources and in lesser 
time. 
Further Recommendation 
3.1.3 The Committee expresses its disappointment over the inordinate delay in finalizing the 
software. It is unfortunate that the Ministry is  still exploring the alternative to develop a less-
costly MIS software. The Committe e calls upon the Ministry to ta ke immediate decision in the 
matter. The Committee however would like to discuss with the officers of the Ministry later. 
3.2 MODERNIZATION OF PRISON ADMINISTRATION 
Recommendation 
3.2.1 T he Committee in its One Hundred and Forty Second Report on Implementation of Central 
Scheme of Modernisation of Prison Administration, made a detailed study of the same and made 
several recommendations for prison infrastructure and correctional administration. The Ministry of 
Home Affairs in its Action Taken Notes stated that the Committee’s recommendations, had been 
forwarded to the State/UT Governments for due compliance and the experience gained during the first 
phase of the implementation of the scheme would be duly utilized in its second phase. The Committee 
found the Action Taken Notes of the Ministry evasive and incomplete and asked the Ministry to furnish 
concrete Action Taken Notes on its recommendations after due consultation with the States/UT 
Governments. While proper Action Taken Notes of the Ministry are still awaited, the Committee is 
surprised to note that the Government has decided to defer the second phase of the scheme while the 
jails in the country, needs immediate modernizat ion. However, the Committee would make detailed 
recommendations on the subject in its Action Taken Report (ATR) after receiving proper Action Taken 
Notes from the Ministry of Home Affairs in the matter. In the meanwhile, the Committee would like the 
Government to reconsider the decision to defer the second phase of the scheme. 

(Para 3.6.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
3.2.2 On the recommendations of the Committee, an Action Taken Note was sent to Rajya Sabha 
Secretariat on 22.07.2009. Since most of the recommendations were related to the States/UTs, 
respective Governments were requested for taking necessary action and furnishing compliance report 
on the recommendations. On the basis of compliance report received from some of the States/UTs, an 
additional ATR has been sent on 19.04.2010 to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat. The remaining State/UT 
Governments have been asked to furnish the compliance report. 
3.2.3 On the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on modernization of 
prisons and also in view of the demands of State Governments, a proposal for second phase of the 
scheme of modernization of prisons was prepared by  the Ministry of Home Affairs. The proposal was 
placed before the Committee of Non-Plan Expenditure (CNE) in Ministry of Finance. It was, however, 
decided that the phase-II of the scheme be deferre d for the time being owing to heavy commitment of 
Government of India on other important sectors. 
3.2.4 The matter was reconsidered in this Ministry  and it has been decided to close the scheme. 
Further Recommendation 
3.2.5 The Committee is constrained to note that the important scheme for modernizing prisons 
in the country is not being given the importance it deserves. It is unfortunate that Government 
has decided to close the scheme. From the point of view of improving the facilities in the prisons, 
it is necessary to have such a scheme as States  will not be implementing such a scheme on their 
own. The Committee desires that Government may reconsider its decision and inform it of its 
decision.
